##### 14.15.8.1 The four-sector singularity catalogue: physics survey

A corrected survey of where mathematical physics worries about singularities. The thermodynamic sector, contrary to a common impression, has a substantial singularity catalogue that the orthodox tradition has engaged with for over a century.

*General relativity.* The Penrose 1965 singularity theorem [281] established that, under generic energy conditions and the existence of a closed trapped surface, gravitational collapse forces a singularity (geodesic incompleteness). The Hawking 1967 cosmological singularity theorem [282] established the past-incompleteness of cosmologically reasonable spacetimes; the Hawking-Penrose 1970 theorem [124] extends both to a single canonical statement. Standard examples — Schwarzschild r = 0 with Kretschmann scalar K = R_μνρσ R^μνρσ = 48 G² M² / (c⁴ r⁶) → ∞; FLRW a(t) → 0 with energy density → ∞ — exhibit the divergence explicitly. These are generic consequences of the Einstein equation under reasonable energy conditions.

*Navier-Stokes.* Leray 1934 [*Acta Math.* 63, 193–248] established the existence of weak global solutions for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on ℝ³ but left open whether these are smooth. The Beale-Kato-Majda 1984 [*Comm. Math. Phys.* 94, 61–66] criterion identifies the vorticity ω = ∇ × **u** as the controlling quantity: blow-up at time T* if and only if ∫₀^{T*} ‖ω(·, t)‖_∞ dt = ∞. Tao 2007 [287] supplied candidate blow-up mechanisms within the continuum theory, identifying specific Navier-Stokes-like systems where blow-up provably occurs. Whether blow-up can occur for the actual Navier-Stokes equations from smooth initial data is the Clay Millennium Problem. Numerical and analytical evidence is suggestive in both directions; the question is open.

*QFT.* Ultraviolet divergences in loop integrals: ∫d⁴k / (k² − m²)² diverges logarithmically; ∫d⁴k · k² / (k² − m²)² diverges quadratically; and so on through the renormalisation-group taxonomy of divergence types. These are routine in perturbative QFT and require regularisation (cutoff Λ, dimensional d = 4 − ε, Pauli-Villars, lattice) plus renormalisation to extract finite predictions. The status: divergent expressions appearing as artefacts of the continuum-field assumption applied to all scales.

*Thermodynamics, three species.* The thermodynamic sector has its own substantial singularity catalogue:

(i) *Critical-point singularities at second-order phase transitions.* At the critical point of water (T_c = 647 K, P_c = 22.1 MPa), the Curie point of a ferromagnet, the superfluid lambda transition of ⁴He at T_λ = 2.17 K, and the Bose-Einstein condensation transition, multiple thermodynamic quantities exhibit power-law divergences: the correlation length ξ ~ |T − T_c|^(−ν) diverges; the specific heat c_V ~ |T − T_c|^(−α) diverges with critical exponent α; the magnetic susceptibility χ ~ |T − T_c|^(−γ) diverges with exponent γ; the order parameter approaches zero with exponent β. The critical exponents satisfy scaling relations (Widom, Fisher, Rushbrooke) and define universality classes. Wilson's renormalization-group machinery (1971 [283], building on Kadanoff 1966 [284] block-spin construction) was developed specifically to handle these divergences — it is the canonical orthodox response to thermodynamic singularities.

(ii) *Black-hole endpoint singularity.* The Hawking temperature T_H = ℏ c³/(8πGMk_B) for a black hole of mass M exhibits T_H → ∞ as M → 0. The semiclassical Hawking-radiation analysis [65] (Hawking 1975) breaks down at M ~ M_Planck with no orthodox identification of the source. The endpoint of black-hole evaporation is one of the canonical unresolved questions of theoretical physics.

(iii) *Third-law approach to T = 0.* As T → 0, multiple thermodynamic quantities exhibit non-analytic limits: heat capacities approach zero with characteristic power laws (c_V ~ T³ for phonons, c_V ~ T for free fermions, c_V ~ T^{3/2} for magnons); the third law (Nernst's heat theorem) constrains the approach to be asymptotic over infinite time, but specific response functions develop singularities or zeros at T = 0 in characteristic patterns.

The thermodynamic singularity catalogue is therefore not "essentially absent." It is the orthodox tradition's most thoroughly developed singularity-handling sector, with Wilson's RG machinery as the most successful unified resolution mechanism. The question is how the four sectors of physics share a unified source.

##### 14.15.8.2 Macroscopic Transport Equations and Parabolic Smoothing Under dx₄/dt = ic: Three Layers That Preserve Transport Thermodynamics from Blow-Up, with the Scope Caveat for Critical-Point Singularities

The reason that *macroscopic transport equations* of thermodynamics — Fourier's heat equation, the diffusion equation, the Fokker-Planck equation, the Boltzmann transport equation, the Navier-Stokes equations specialised to thermal sectors — exhibit no finite-time blow-up has three layers, each, with the explicit qualification that the layered protection covers transport dynamics but does not extend to critical-point singularities (which are equilibrium-thermodynamic phenomena at fixed T near T_c, not transport phenomena).

*Layer 1: Parabolic equations have the smoothing property.* The heat equation ∂_t T = κ ∇² T, the Fokker-Planck equation, and other thermodynamic transport equations are parabolic in the standard PDE classification (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, 2nd ed., 2010, §2.3 and §7.1). For parabolic equations with bounded initial data, the maximum principle (Evans §7.1.4) bounds the solution at all later times by the initial maximum, and standard heat-kernel regularity (Evans §V.2.3.1) gives analytic solutions for any t > 0 regardless of how rough the initial data is. The heat kernel K(**x**, t) = (4π κ t)^(−d/2) exp(−|**x**|² / 4κt) is C^∞ for any t > 0 and any spatial dimension d. Even initial data as singular as δ(**x**) is smoothed to an analytic Gaussian within an arbitrarily short time. Singularities in initial conditions are dissipated, not amplified; gradients decrease monotonically in the L² sense via the dissipation identity d/dt ∫|∇T|² dx ≤ 0.

*Layer 2: The Second Law actively prevents gradient sharpening as a dynamical statement.* The Second Law dS/dt ≥ 0, with strict positivity in non-equilibrium configurations, is the dynamical statement that entropy production accompanies all irreversible processes. Boltzmann's H-theorem (Boltzmann 1872; standard treatment in K. Huang, *Statistical Mechanics*, 2nd ed., 1987, §4.1) establishes dH/dt ≤ 0 for the Boltzmann H-functional H[f] = ∫f log f d³**v**, with strict inequality unless f is the local Maxwell-Boltzmann equilibrium distribution. The entropy production rate σ = ∑_i J_i · X_i (fluxes times conjugate forces, per de Groot-Mazur, *Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics*, 1962, §III) is non-negative quadratic in the gradients. As gradients sharpen, entropy production increases, and the entropy-production accumulation forces the gradients to soften: the Second Law is the *active smoothing* of would-be singular configurations in transport dynamics.

*Layer 3: Thermodynamic variables are by construction coarse-grained.* Temperature T, entropy S, pressure P, density ρ are averages over many microscopic degrees of freedom. The thermodynamic-limit construction (taking the number of particles N → ∞ at fixed N/V, the standard procedure of statistical mechanics) builds the averaging in at the level of variables. Fourier's law ∂_t T = κ ∇² T explicitly carries information about the underlying microphysics via the diffusion coefficient κ, which has dimensions of [length]²/[time] and is set by the mean free path λ_mfp and thermal speed v_th of the constituent microparticles via κ ~ λ_mfp · v_th / 3. Fourier's law has a built-in domain of validity: gradients on scales >> λ_mfp; it breaks down (in the standard reading) when gradient scales approach λ_mfp, and the breakdown is recognised and expected.

These three layers cover macroscopic transport dynamics. They do not cover critical-point singularities, which arise at *equilibrium* configurations (fixed T, P at T = T_c) where transport dynamics is irrelevant and the divergence is in the equilibrium correlation functions themselves. Wilson's RG handles critical-point singularities by a different mechanism: rescaling the equilibrium theory through successive block-spin transformations and identifying the divergence as the flow toward a non-trivial fixed point under the rescaling. The mechanism is analogous to QFT renormalization, which is the orthodox-tradition identification (Wilson 1971) of QFT UV and critical-point thermodynamics as one phenomenon.

The corrected picture: transport thermodynamics has parabolic-smoothing protection from finite-time blow-up; equilibrium-critical thermodynamics has divergences that the orthodox tradition handles by Wilson RG; black-hole-endpoint and third-law singularities are boundary phenomena at scales where the macroscopic thermodynamic description fails for McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold-microphysical reasons. The thermodynamic sector is therefore richer in singularity content than either GR, Navier-Stokes, or QFT individually — but it is the sector where the orthodox unified resolution mechanism (Wilson RG) was first established.

##### 14.15.8.3 Wilson's renormalization-group construction: the orthodox identification of QFT ultraviolet divergences and critical-point thermodynamics as one phenomenon

Wilson 1971 [283] established a identification that matters for the unified four-sector resolution. The Wilson renormalization-group construction operates as follows: at each step, integrate out high-momentum (short-wavelength) field modes between an upper cutoff Λ and a lower cutoff Λ/b for some rescaling factor b > 1, then rescale lengths by factor b to restore the original cutoff. The successive rescalings define a flow on the space of effective theories; fixed points of the flow describe scale-invariant theories; the flow near a fixed point in stable directions defines a renormalizable theory.

*The critical-point reading.* At a second-order phase transition (e.g., the Ising critical point), the correlation length ξ diverges; the theory is scale-invariant in the long-wavelength limit. The Wilson RG flow has a non-trivial fixed point (the Wilson-Fisher fixed point in 4 − ε dimensions) controlling the critical behaviour, with the critical exponents α, β, γ, δ, ν computable from the eigenvalues of the linearised RG flow at the fixed point. The orthodox handling of critical-point divergences is therefore the identification of these divergences as manifestations of the system's approach to a non-trivial RG fixed point in the long-wavelength limit.

*The QFT-UV reading.* In perturbative QFT, loop integrals ∫d⁴k F(k) diverge at k → ∞ because the field theory's integration extends to arbitrarily short wavelengths. The Wilson RG construction handles this by treating the QFT as the long-wavelength limit of a more fundamental theory with a UV cutoff: the divergences are artefacts of taking the cutoff to infinity, and the predictive content of the theory is the flow of effective couplings under the rescaling, expressed via beta functions β(g) = μ dg/dμ. Asymptotic-freedom theories (QCD via Gross-Wilczek-Politzer 1973) have UV fixed points at g* = 0; asymptotically-safe theories (Weinberg's program, §14.15.8.4 below) have non-trivial UV fixed points at g* ≠ 0.

*The identification.* The two readings are the same construction. The Wilson RG operates on the space of effective theories irrespective of whether the theory describes critical thermodynamics or QFT loop integrals; the long-wavelength behaviour at critical points and the short-wavelength behaviour of QFT both reduce to questions about the RG flow's fixed-point structure. Wilson 1971 explicitly noted the identification: the renormalization group as developed for critical phenomena applies equally to quantum field theory, and the divergences in both sectors arise from the same continuum-limit phenomenon. Kadanoff's 1966 block-spin construction [284] supplied the conceptual precursor by showing how successive block averaging on an Ising lattice produces the rescaling flow that Wilson made systematic.

The punchline: the orthodox tradition has already identified two of the four sectors (QFT UV and critical-point thermodynamics) as the same phenomenon, with the Wilson-Kadanoff RG construction as the unified handling mechanism. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's contribution to the unification extends the identification to all four sectors (adding GR singularities and Navier-Stokes blow-up) and supplies the principle (the McGucken Sphere mode count) that the RG construction has been waiting on as the source of the natural cutoff.

The answer is that all three objections were designed to rule out *one specific picture*: a globally-defined spatial lattice with discrete points in all three spatial dimensions, treated as the metric structure of the Manifold. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold has a different architecture: continuous ℝ³ in the spatial 3-slice, with discrete ℓ_P · ℤ in the x₄ direction only, and the x₄-tick structure attached to the fiber over each event rather than to a global background. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's spatial structure is *not* a lattice in the sense required by any of the three objections. The dual-channel Reciprocal Generation reading (§3.2 above; [76, §14.10–14.12]) supplies the mechanism by which the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's asymmetric discreteness coexists with exact Lorentz invariance and supports the chiral fermion content of the Standard Model. This subsection develops the engagement explicitly.

##### 14.15.9.1 Weyl's tile argument and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's continuous spatial 3-slice

Weyl 1949 [288] (*Philosophy of Mathematics and Natural Science*, Princeton University Press) presented the argument against discrete spatial structure as follows. Suppose physical space is a discrete grid of tiles of side length a, with distance measured by tile-counting along grid-aligned directions. Consider a square region of side length n · a (n tiles per side). Along either side, the distance is n · a; along the diagonal, the discrete tile-counting metric gives the same distance n · a (one step diagonal = one step along either axis at the level of tile-counting), not √2 · n · a as the Pythagorean theorem demands. The argument generalises to rotational invariance: a rod of length L aligned with the grid contains L/a tiles; the same rod rotated by 45° contains a different number of tiles along its length under tile-counting, so the rod's measured length changes with rotation angle. Weyl concluded that physical space cannot be a discrete grid.

The argument's actual scope is narrower than commonly understood. The conclusion follows only when three conditions are satisfied jointly:

(W1) The discrete structure is in the *spatial dimensions* (the three directions in which measuring rods extend).

(W2) The discrete structure is *the physical metric* — that is, distances are computed by tile-counting on the discrete structure itself, not by an underlying continuous metric defined independently of the discrete structure.

(W3) The discreteness operates at a scale comparable to or coarser than the scale of measurement, so that the discrete structure is visible to the measurement apparatus.

Any picture failing at least one of (W1), (W2), (W3) is not ruled out by Weyl's argument. Modern circumvention strategies in the literature each relax exactly one of these conditions: lattice QCD relaxes (W3) by sending the lattice spacing to zero in the continuum limit; spin-foam approaches relax (W1) by having combinatorial structure that is not a spatial grid; quantum-graph models relax (W2) by separating the combinatorial structure from the metric. See Hagar 2014 [293] (*Discrete or Continuous? The Quest for Fundamental Length in Modern Physics*, Cambridge University Press) for a comprehensive survey of the Weyl argument's scope, its assumptions, and the responses to it in modern fundamental physics. None of the surveyed approaches has the specific position of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, which violates all three conditions simultaneously and through facts rather than calculational devices.

*The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position relative to (W1).* The spatial 3-slice of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold is continuous ℝ³, by the construction of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold measure ℳ = ℝ³ × (ℓ_P · ℤ) per Theorem 3.5. The three spatial directions x₁, x₂, x₃ have no tile structure of any kind; spatial separations are measured by the continuous Euclidean distance on the spatial 3-slice (in the rest frame; the Lorentzian metric ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt² applies in the relativistic generalisation). The Pythagorean theorem a² + b² = c² holds exactly on the spatial 3-slice. The diagonal of an n × n square has length √2 · n by continuous Euclidean geometry, not n by tile-counting. Condition (W1) is violated: there is no spatial-dimension discreteness on the Manifold.

*The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position relative to (W2).* The Lorentzian metric ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt² is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's continuous metric structure (the Algebraic Channel reading, §3.2 above), with the i² = −1 of Frobenius's theorem on real division algebras supplying the algebra of the time-direction signature flip per [76, §14.6 Signature-Bridging Theorem] and the Lorentzian signature being a theorem rather than a postulate. Physical distances are computed via this continuous metric on the spatial 3-slice, not by tile-counting on the discrete x₄ structure. The discrete x₄ structure at ℓ_P is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's UV-completion content (the source of the Planck-scale mode count N(A) = A · c³/(πℏG) that resolves the four pathology sectors of §14.15.8 above), not the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's metric structure. Condition (W2) is violated: the discrete x₄ structure is not the physical metric; the continuous Lorentzian metric is.

*The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position relative to (W3).* The Planck-tick scale ℓ_P = √(ℏG/c³) ~ 1.6 × 10^{−35} m is twenty-five orders of magnitude below atomic measurement scales (~10^{−10} m), sixteen orders of magnitude below the smallest experimentally probed scales (LHC and beyond at ~10^{−19} m), and twenty orders of magnitude below the proton's charge radius (~10^{−15} m). The discrete structure at ℓ_P is not visible to any experimentally accessible measurement apparatus; any measuring rod sees only the continuous Lorentzian metric to extraordinary precision. Condition (W3) is violated: the discreteness is below all accessible measurement scales by twenty-plus orders of magnitude.

*Beyond the three conditions: the per-event-not-global structure of the Manifold's discreteness.* The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework violates Weyl's three conditions even before reaching the deepest difference. The discrete x₄ structure at ℓ_P is per-event: each event in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold has its own x₄-tick structure attached to its fiber, not to a global background lattice. A measuring rod in spatial 3-slice motion does not encounter a global tile-grid at any orientation; the rod's spatial 3-slice motion is on the continuous ℝ³ base manifold, while the per-event x₄-ticks live in the fiber over each event. The standard rotational-invariance worry of Weyl's argument — that a rod changes length under rotation because it changes which tiles it sits on — does not apply because there are no tiles for the rod to sit on. The rod sits on the continuous ℝ³ base manifold; rotation acts by SO(3) on the spatial 3-slice; the per-event x₄-tick structure rotates with the rod under SO(3) action by Reciprocal Generation between Algebraic Channel (SO(3) symmetry of the spatial slice) and Geometric Channel (per-event Sphere expansion that respects SO(3) by construction).

The Weyl tile argument therefore fails to apply to the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold at every level: spatial structure is continuous (W1 violated); the discrete structure is not the metric (W2 violated); the discrete scale is twenty-five orders of magnitude below measurement scales (W3 violated); and the deepest level — per-event rather than global discreteness — moots even the rotational-invariance concern that motivates Weyl's worry. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not need to evade Weyl's argument through a clever loophole; it has a different architecture that the argument does not address.

##### 14.15.9.2 Lorentz invariance and the per-event x₄-tick structure

The Lorentz invariance objection to discrete-spacetime models is the most experimentally constraining of the three discrete-spacetime objections. The argument: any global spatial lattice introduces a preferred reference frame (the lattice rest frame, in which all lattice translations are pure spatial translations); particle dispersion relations on a lattice contain higher-order terms (typically sin²(p · a/2) corrections in place of the continuum p² term) that produce direction-dependent and frame-dependent effects; these effects are testable via cosmic-ray observations, GRB photon arrival times, atom-clock comparisons, and other high-precision measurements. Coleman-Glashow 1999 [290] (*Phys. Rev. D* 59, 116008) initiated the systematic high-energy Lorentz-test programme; Mattingly 2005 [291] (*Living Rev. Relativity* 8, 5) and Liberati 2013 [292] (*Class. Quant. Grav.* 30, 133001) supply comprehensive reviews. Current experimental bounds on Lorentz-violation operators are extraordinarily tight at scales approaching ℓ_P: bounds on dimension-5 Lorentz-violation operators in the photon sector are better than 1 part in 10¹⁹ from GRB photon arrival times (Vasileiou et al. 2013, *Phys. Rev. D* 87, 122001); bounds on dimension-4 operators are at the 1 part in 10²² level from astrophysical observations. Any framework with global spatial-lattice structure at the Planck scale would generically predict Lorentz-violation operators at observable levels and would be ruled out by these bounds.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold is *not* a global spatial lattice. Spatial 3-slice is continuous ℝ³; only the x₄ fiber over each event has the ℓ_P · ℤ discrete structure. The question is whether this asymmetric discreteness, with per-event-not-global x₄-ticks, preserves exact Lorentz invariance or introduces Lorentz-violation operators.

The answer is precise: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework preserves exact Lorentz invariance, by the dual-channel Reciprocal Generation reading that is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's deepest fact. The argument has two parts: a Algebraic Channel reading and a Geometric Channel reading, which must be developed together.

*Algebraic Channel reading: the Lorentzian manifold and the Poincaré algebra.* Algebraic Channel (the algebraic-symmetry channel; §3.2 above, §14.10 of [76]) sees the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold as a continuous Lorentzian manifold ℝ^{1,3} with metric ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt². The full Poincaré algebra acts exactly: translations P_μ generate spacetime translations; rotations J_i and boosts K_i generate the Lorentz subalgebra SO(3,1). The Lorentzian metric emerges from the algebraic operation i² = −1 applied to the x₄ direction via x₄ = ict, with the signature flip being the Signature-Bridging Theorem [76, §14.6] from Frobenius's theorem on real division algebras [76, §14.12.4 Forcing 1]. Algebraic Channel's content is fully Lorentz-invariant; there is no preferred frame and no global lattice in Algebraic Channel's reading.

*Geometric Channel reading: per-event Sphere expansion with no preferred frame.* Geometric Channel (the geometric-propagation channel) sees the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold as a collection of per-event McGucken Spheres Σ_+(p), each expanding at velocity c from its apex event with isotropic SO(3) symmetry in the local spatial 3-slice and +ic monotonicity in the x₄ direction by the +ic direction at every event. The per-event Sphere structure is not relative to a globally-preferred frame: each event has its own local rest frame defined by its own Sphere apex; Lorentz boosts relate the per-event Sphere structures of events at different velocities by the same Lorentz boost. There is no globally-preferred frame anywhere in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold; each event carries its own +ic-direction, and the +ic-directions of two events related by a Lorentz boost are related by the same Lorentz boost (with the boost acting on x₄-direction unit vectors in the standard Lorentz-covariant manner).

The physical fact: **the x₄-direction discreteness at ℓ_P is per-event in the fiber direction, not global in a background lattice**. Each event has its own x₄-tick structure attached to its fiber; the ticks of two events related by a Lorentz boost are related by the same boost; the discreteness is in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's fiber structure (the x₄ axis at each event), not in a globally-fixed lattice over the base manifold. This is analogous to how a fiber bundle can have discrete fibers without imposing a preferred section over the base: the discrete structure lives in the fibers, the base manifold remains continuous, and any symmetry that acts continuously on the base extends to act on the fiber bundle without breaking the discreteness.

The comparison with standard discrete-spacetime models is sharp. Lattice QCD imposes a single global lattice that defines preferred directions and a preferred rest frame (the lattice rest frame); Lorentz boost invariance is broken by the lattice spacing in the standard Wilson, staggered, and domain-wall formulations, with the broken invariance being recovered only in the continuum limit a → 0. Causal set theory has discrete events but a global causal-set ordering that picks out a preferred way of decomposing spacetime into past and future; modifications of Lorentz invariance have been studied in this framework with constraints from observational bounds. Loop quantum gravity has discrete area and volume spectra defined in a globally-defined kinematical Hilbert space; the question of whether this discrete structure is compatible with exact Lorentz invariance at the dynamical level (the "Lorentz invariance vs. minimum length" puzzle in LQG) has been a longstanding open question. All three approaches face the Lorentz-violation problem at observational scales because all three have some form of *global* discrete structure that breaks Lorentz boost invariance.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold has no global discreteness. The Manifold measure ℳ = ℝ³ × (ℓ_P · ℤ) is the measure on the *fiber over each event*, not the measure on a global background. The Pontryagin dual ℳ̂ = ℝ³ × 𝕋_{ℓ_P} (Folland 2016 Theorem 4.31; §3.7 above) has compact dual 𝕋_{ℓ_P} for the discrete x₄ direction, which is the source of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's Brillouin-Zone Support and the UV finiteness of loop integrals (resolution R1 of Theorem 14.15.8 above). The compactness lives in the fiber direction over each event; Lorentz boosts act on the spatial 3-slice and on the x₄ direction in a Lorentz-covariant manner; the discrete-x₄-fiber structure transforms covariantly under Lorentz boost because each event's x₄-tick is the per-event of forward +ic-expansion, and Lorentz boost relates the per-event +ic-directions of different events by the standard Lorentz transformation law on four-vectors.

*The diagnosis of why the per-event-fiber structure preserves Lorentz invariance.* The Lorentz-violation operators that arise in standard discrete-spacetime models come from the dispersion-relation corrections sin²(p · a/2) that replace the continuum p² term when the lattice spacing a is finite. These corrections introduce direction-dependence (different lattice axes give different sin² corrections) and frame-dependence (Lorentz boosting the dispersion relation does not preserve the sin² form). On the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold, the dispersion relation has the form

with k₄ ∈ 𝔹 the Brillouin-zone variable from §3.7 above (cited at §3.8 of this paper). The sin² correction here is *only* in the k₄ direction, not in the spatial momentum components p₁, p₂, p₃. Spatial momentum components retain the continuum dispersion |p|² c² with no correction. The dispersion relation is *rotationally invariant* (SO(3) acts only on the spatial p variables, leaving them with continuum dispersion) and *Lorentz-boost invariant* in a specific way that requires the dual-channel reading to articulate.

The Lorentz-boost invariance argument runs as follows. A Lorentz boost by velocity v in the x₁ direction acts on the spatial-momentum and energy variables in the standard Lorentz-covariant way: p₁ → γ(p₁ − vE/c²), E → γ(E − vp₁). The k₄ variable, by the +ic direction at every event (+ic monotonicity per event), is the per-event of forward x₄-expansion at rate ic; under Lorentz boost, the per-event +ic-direction of each event transforms by the same Lorentz boost (because Algebraic Channel's Lorentzian metric and Geometric Channel's per-event +ic-direction are Reciprocally Generated from the same dx₄/dt = ic at every event, with the Lorentz boost acting on both consistently). The dispersion relation is therefore Lorentz-covariant: each event's local rest frame sees the per-event dispersion with k₄ in the Brillouin zone of that event's fiber, and Lorentz-boosted observers see Lorentz-boosted versions of the same dispersion. No preferred frame is selected; no Lorentz-violation operators arise; the experimental bounds on Lorentz-violation operators are automatically satisfied.

*Comparison with the Lorentz-invariant noncommutative-geometry literature.* The κ-deformed Poincaré algebra (Lukierski et al. 1991, *Phys. Lett. B* 264, 331; Majid-Ruegg 1994, *Phys. Lett. B* 334, 348) and the related Doubly Special Relativity (DSR; Amelino-Camelia 2002, *Phys. Lett. B* 510, 255; Magueijo-Smolin 2002, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 88, 190403) explored ways to introduce a Planck-scale invariant length while preserving (or deforming) Lorentz invariance. ##### 14.15.9.3 The Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's non-lattice Manifold

The Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem (Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981 [289], *Nucl. Phys. B* 185, 20 and *Nucl. Phys. B* 193, 173) is the most mathematically rigorous of the three discrete-spacetime objections. The theorem states: any lattice formulation of fermion field theory satisfying five precise axioms must contain an equal number of left-handed and right-handed fermion species (the "fermion-doubling problem"). The Standard Model's chiral structure — left-handed fermions in SU(2)_L doublets, right-handed fermions as SU(2) singlets, with the W^± and Z bosons coupling only to left-handed components — cannot be obtained from a Nielsen-Ninomiya-compatible lattice. This is a genuine theorem, and it is a real obstruction for any framework that proposes to UV-complete the Standard Model via a spatial lattice.

The five Nielsen-Ninomiya axioms (Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981 [289], stated in their canonical form):

(NN1) *Locality*: the lattice action couples only finitely many lattice sites (more precisely, the Fourier transform of the lattice action is analytic in the lattice momentum, equivalent to exponentially-bounded coupling in lattice position space).

(NN2) *Hermiticity*: the lattice action is Hermitian (giving a positive-definite probability interpretation).

(NN3) *Translational invariance on the lattice*: the action is invariant under integer translations of the lattice — that is, T_n ψ(x) = ψ(x + n · a) is a symmetry for all integers n.

(NN4) *Chiral charge conservation*: γ⁵ commutes with the Dirac operator (equivalently, the U(1) chiral symmetry of the continuum theory is preserved on the lattice).

(NN5) *Bilinear quadratic action*: the action is quadratic in the fermion fields ψ, ψ̄.

The theorem's statement: under (NN1)–(NN5), the number of fermion zero modes on the lattice must be even, with equal numbers of left-handed and right-handed components — the doubling. The Wilson, staggered, domain-wall, and overlap fermion formulations each violate one of (NN3) or (NN4) to circumvent the doubling: Wilson fermions violate (NN4) by adding a symmetry-breaking Wilson term; staggered fermions reduce the doubling factor from 16 to 4 by distributing components over the lattice while still violating (NN4) in a controlled way; domain-wall fermions violate (NN3) effectively by extending into a fifth dimension; overlap fermions satisfy the Ginsparg-Wilson relation (Ginsparg-Wilson 1982 [294], *Phys. Rev. D* 25, 2649) which gives an approximate chiral symmetry on the lattice without exact violation of (NN4), but the construction is computationally intensive and faces subtleties at the multi-flavour level.

*The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position relative to (NN1)–(NN5).* The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold satisfies (NN1) at the Manifold level: McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold actions couple events to nearby events through Geometric Channel Sphere expansion at finite rate c, with the per-event Sphere having compact support on the local light cone. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework satisfies (NN2): Manifold actions are Hermitian by construction (the Dirac action of the standard kind has its Hermiticity-preserving structure on the continuous spatial 3-slice). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework satisfies (NN5): the standard fermion action of the Standard Model is bilinear quadratic in ψ, ψ̄.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position on (NN3) — the axiom — is that *the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold is not a spatial lattice in the Nielsen-Ninomiya sense*. Axiom (NN3) requires the existence of a global spatial lattice with integer-translation symmetry; the action's invariance under T_n ψ(x) = ψ(x + n · a) for all integers n requires that the lattice itself is a globally-defined object in the spatial dimensions. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold has continuous ℝ³ in the spatial dimensions; spatial translations are continuous translations, not integer translations on a lattice. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework satisfies the *continuous* translation invariance of the spatial 3-slice (the full ℝ³ translation group acts), not the *discrete* integer-translation invariance that (NN3) requires.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's discrete x₄ structure does have integer-translation invariance in the fiber direction over each event (the ℓ_P · ℤ translation group acts on each event's x₄ fiber), but this is per-event-in-the-fiber, not the global spatial lattice that (NN3) requires. The Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem analyses lattices that are globally-defined in the spatial directions; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold has continuous spatial directions with discreteness only in the temporal-perpendicular x₄ fiber over each event. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not satisfy (NN3) in the sense Nielsen-Ninomiya require; the theorem's hypotheses are not met; the theorem's conclusion (forced fermion doubling) does not apply.

*The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position on (NN4).* The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives the chiral structure of the Standard Model as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic per [3 Parts I–IV] and §9 of this paper. The SU(2)_L gauge group is theorem-derived; left-handed fermions appearing in SU(2)_L doublets and right-handed fermions appearing as SU(2) singlets is the theorem-derived chiral structure. The U(1) chiral symmetry γ⁵-conservation is a continuum statement that applies on the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's continuous spatial 3-slice; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold does not impose a γ⁵-violating Wilson-style term because the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold is not a spatial lattice in the first place.

*The diagnosis.* The Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem is a real theorem with rigorously stated axioms, and the theorem genuinely rules out chiral fermions on Nielsen-Ninomiya-compatible spatial lattices. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold is not a spatial lattice in the Nielsen-Ninomiya sense; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's discreteness is one-dimensional (in x₄ only) and per-event-in-the-fiber (not global in the base), neither of which is the picture the theorem addresses. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's chiral fermion content of the Standard Model — left-handed SU(2)_L doublets, right-handed singlets, with the parity-violating weak interaction — is theorem-derived in [3 Parts I–IV] and §9 of this paper, with the chiral structure descending from dx₄/dt = ic's Manifold-level without invoking any lattice structure that the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem would obstruct.

*Comparison with the Ginsparg-Wilson and domain-wall approaches.* The Ginsparg-Wilson relation (Ginsparg-Wilson 1982 [294]) and the overlap fermion formulation (Neuberger 1998, *Phys. Lett. B* 417, 141) provide approximate chiral symmetry on the lattice by replacing the exact (NN4) γ⁵-commutativity with the milder Ginsparg-Wilson relation {D, γ⁵} = a · D γ⁵ D for lattice spacing a. The construction recovers chiral symmetry in the continuum limit and provides a practically successful framework for chiral lattice QCD, but the formulation is computationally expensive (matrix sign-function calculations) and has subtleties at the multi-flavour and topological levels. The domain-wall fermion approach (Kaplan 1992; Shamir 1993, *Nucl. Phys. B* 406, 90) puts the chiral fermions on the boundary of a five-dimensional lattice, recovering chirality in the limit where the fifth-dimension extent goes to infinity. Both approaches are workarounds to the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction within the spatial-lattice paradigm; neither matches the position of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, which simply does not have spatial-lattice structure and therefore does not face the obstruction in the first place.

##### 14.15.9.4 summary: asymmetric discreteness, Reciprocal Generation, and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's distinctive position

The position of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework with respect to the three discrete-spacetime no-go arguments can be stated cleanly:

(a) *Spatial 3-slice continuous.* The three spatial directions x₁, x₂, x₃ are continuous ℝ³. No tile structure of any kind. Pythagorean theorem holds exactly. Rotation acts by exact SO(3) on the spatial 3-slice. Weyl's tile argument does not apply: spatial structure is not discrete in the sense Weyl addresses (W1 violated), the metric is not tile-counting (W2 violated), and the only discrete McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold structure lives at twenty-five orders of magnitude below measurement scales (W3 violated).

(b) *x₄ direction discrete at ℓ_P, per-event in the fiber.* The x₄ direction has ℓ_P · ℤ structure attached to the fiber over each event, not to a global background. The discreteness is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's UV-completion content (resolving the four sectors of continuum-approximation pathology of §14.15.8 above), not a global lattice. Lorentz boosts act on the per-event +ic-direction in the standard Lorentz-covariant manner; the discrete-x₄-fiber structure transforms covariantly with the boost; no preferred frame is introduced; experimental bounds on Lorentz-violation operators are automatically satisfied.

(c) *Dispersion relation Lorentz-covariant.* The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold dispersion E² = c² p² + (2ℏc/ℓ_P)² sin²(k₄ ℓ_P / 2ℏ) + m² c⁴ has continuum dispersion in the spatial-momentum directions and sin² correction only in the k₄ direction over each event. Spatial isotropy SO(3) is exact; Lorentz boost invariance is exact via Reciprocal Generation between Algebraic Channel's continuous Lorentzian manifold and Geometric Channel's per-event Sphere expansion.

(d) *Chiral fermions theorem-derived without lattice obstruction.* The Standard Model's chiral structure (left-handed SU(2)_L doublets, right-handed singlets) is theorem-derived from dx₄/dt = ic per [3 Parts I–IV] and §9 of this paper. The Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem does not apply because the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold is not a spatial lattice in the Nielsen-Ninomiya sense; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's discreteness is one-dimensional in x₄ and per-event-in-the-fiber, neither of which is the picture the theorem addresses.

(e) *Reciprocal Generation supplies the mechanism.* The dual-channel architecture (§1.2 above, [76, §14.10–14.12]) coordinates Algebraic Channel's continuous-Lorentzian-manifold reading and Geometric Channel's per-event-Sphere-expansion reading to deliver simultaneously exact Lorentz invariance and Planck-scale UV cutoff content. The two readings are the same McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold viewed through complementary lenses; the Reciprocal Generation between them is what allows the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework to have UV-cutoff content without spatial-discreteness content, exact Lorentz invariance without κ-deformation of the Poincaré algebra, and chiral fermions without lattice-doubling obstruction.

The three discrete-spacetime no-go arguments — Weyl's tile argument (1949 [288]), the Lorentz-invariance tests (Coleman-Glashow 1999 [290]; Mattingly 2005 [291]; Liberati 2013 [292]), the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem (1981 [289]) — were each designed to rule out frameworks with global spatial-lattice structure. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework has fundamentally different architecture: asymmetric discreteness (continuous spatial 3-slice, discrete x₄ fiber), per-event-not-global fiber structure, dual-channel Reciprocal Generation reading. None of the three no-go arguments addresses the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's actual position; each presupposes a global spatial lattice that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not have. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's resolution of the four sectors of continuum-approximation pathology in §14.15.8 above — via the McGucken Sphere mode count operating at the bi-scale Planck and molecular cutoffs — therefore proceeds without running into any of the standard no-go obstructions to discrete-spacetime models. The discreteness that supplies the UV cutoff is different from the discreteness that the no-go arguments rule out, and the dual-channel architecture is what makes this difference rather than coincidental.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's position on discrete-spacetime no-go arguments is therefore not "discrete spacetime with a clever workaround." #### 14.17.8 Direction B Under dx₄/dt = ic: Sharp Contrast with Kaluza-Klein Compactification Programmes — McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold x₄-Discretization Is Not a Compactified Extra Dimension

Kaluza–Klein programmes (T. Kaluza 1921, O. Klein 1926, and subsequent developments including string-theoretic compactification) generate gauge symmetries by starting with a higher-dimensional total space, adding one or more compact extra dimensions, and identifying the gauge group with the isometry group of the compact fiber. In the simplest case, adding an S¹ (compact circle) of small radius R gives U(1) as the isometry group of the fiber, and the metric decomposes into a 4D metric plus a U(1) gauge field plus a scalar (dilaton). This is the "Kaluza miracle" — the higher-dimensional scalar curvature reduces to Einstein–Hilbert plus Maxwell action.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's contrast with Kaluza–Klein is specific:

**(K-1) No extra dimensions.** The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework has four dimensions total. There is no fifth spatial direction compactified to a circle. The U(1) fiber is the phase-rotation subgroup of the perpendicularity structure of x₄ orthogonal to the three spatial directions.

**(K-2) Same U(1), different substrate origin.** Kaluza–Klein U(1) = isometry group of S¹ fiber. McGucken U(1) = phase-rotation group of x₄-orientation at each event. Both yield the same electromagnetic gauge phenomenology in 4D, but they come from different substrate.

**(K-3) No Kaluza–Klein tower of massive states.** Kaluza–Klein predicts a tower of states with masses m_n = n/R for n ∈ ℤ from momentum quantisation around the compact circle. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework predicts no such tower because there is no compact fiber to have momentum quantised around. The absence of the Kaluza–Klein tower is an empirical prediction that distinguishes the two frameworks (though the tower is also unobserved because R is required to be Planck-scale, so the two frameworks are empirically degenerate at accessible energies).

**(K-4) No dilaton scalar.** Kaluza–Klein necessarily includes a scalar field from the g_{55} component of the higher-dimensional metric (the dilaton, or radion). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework predicts no dilaton because there is no fifth-dimensional metric component. The Higgs field of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework has different substrate: it is the field-theoretic encoding of the +ic direction, not the radion of a compactified fifth dimension.

**(K-5) Gauge group derivation, not postulation.** Kaluza–Klein derives U(1) from the isometry of S¹; extending to non-abelian gauge groups requires compact manifolds with larger isometry groups (e.g., S³ gives SU(2)), which introduces multi-scalar sectors. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives U(1)_Y, SU(2)_L, and SU(3)_c from McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold structure without adding extra dimensions, using the three-perpendicular-sub-spheres structure and the Clifford Weyl-doublet content instead.

#### 14.17.9 Direction B: The connection 1-form as McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold x₄-phase-rotation

An Ehresmann connection on a principal G-bundle is a smooth horizontal distribution H ⊂ TP satisfying the equivariance and reproduction conditions on the fundamental vector field. Equivalently, it is a Lie-algebra-valued 1-form ω ∈ Ω¹(P; 𝔤) satisfying the Kobayashi–Nomizu conditions. The horizontal/vertical decomposition T_pP = H_p ⊕ V_p at each p ∈ P has direct Manifold in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework:

**Vertical direction**: the fiber-direction subspace V_p = ker dπ_p at p corresponds to pure gauge-transformation content — an infinitesimal change in the local x₄-phase (for U(1)) or in the local gauge-frame (for SU(2)_L, SU(3)_c) at the event π(p), with no motion in the base spacetime. The vertical direction is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's local-gauge-rotation at each event.

**Horizontal direction**: the base-direction subspace H_p at p corresponds to McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold propagation — an infinitesimal spacetime translation at π(p) with the chosen local gauge-frame parallel-transported along. The horizontal direction is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's spacetime-propagation, with the parallel-transport specification supplied by the connection.

**Correction to the naive reading**: the vertical direction is *not* motion in the x₄ coordinate itself. Motion in the x₄ coordinate is spacetime motion (base motion), because x₄ = ict is one of the four spacetime coordinates. The vertical direction is *pure x₄-phase rotation at a fixed event* — a rotation in the perpendicular x₄ orthogonal to the local +ic direction, with no spacetime displacement. This distinction matters: the fiber is the phase-rotation group, not the coordinate-translation content.

The connection 1-form ω evaluated on a vector V ∈ T_pP returns the vertical component of V in the fiber-Lie-algebra 𝔤. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold reading, this is the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's accounting of how much of V is pure x₄-phase-rotation (vertical, in 𝔲(1) or 𝔰𝔲(2) or 𝔰𝔲(3)) versus how much is McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold-propagation (horizontal, along the base).

Sections §§14.17.2–14.17.10 treat the base manifold as the smooth Lorentzian spacetime ℳ = ℝ^{1,3}. **At the "long-wavelength" limit**, where the base structure is coarse-grained to smooth Lorentzian spacetime by averaging over scales larger than ℓ_P, all of §§14.17.2–14.17.10 apply directly with the standard machinery. The corpus's bundle-theoretic statements (No-Monopole via Steenrod; No-Domain-Wall via Steenrod; SU(3)_c principal bundle) all operate at this long-wavelength limit. At the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold scale ℓ_P, the bundle-theoretic structure requires the LCA-adapted machinery which is Grade-3 open.

#### 14.17.14 The Reciprocal-Relationship Summary Under dx₄/dt = ic: Direction A (Triviality → No-Monopole) and Direction B (Non-Triviality → Gauge Structure) Are the Two Faces of the Same McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold Bundle

The relationship between fiber bundles and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework can be summarised in three coordinated statements, each stated at the appropriate rigor grade:

**(R-1) Fiber bundles are the correct mathematical vocabulary for the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's gauge-content statements.** Every gauge-theoretic statement the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework makes — A_μ as connection, F as curvature, ⟨H⟩ as section, SU(3)_c as structure group, No-Monopole via Steenrod, Kogut–Susskind plaquette as McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold holonomy — is expressible in bundle language without loss of content. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not require alternative mathematical machinery.

**(R-2) The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the physics that makes bundle theory more than abstract mathematics.** Standard bundle theory postulates structures (base manifold, fiber, structure group, connection). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives specific instances of those structures from dx₄/dt = ic: the U(1) fiber is the x₄-phase-rotation group; the SU(2)_L fiber comes from Sphere SO(3) on Clifford Weyl doublets; the SU(3)_c fiber comes from three-perpendicular-sub-spheres; the electroweak bundle is trivial because the Higgs supplies a global +ic-pointer section; the Standard Model gauge group is Inn(𝒜_F)/centre for a McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold-derived internal algebra. This is a substantial reduction in postulated content: from "Standard Model gauge group as empirical input to bundle theory" to "Standard Model gauge group as derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic expressed in bundle language."

**(R-3) The relationship is complementary, not competitive.** Fiber-bundle theory is exactly right at what it does — supplying the mathematical formal language for local-and-global gauge content on manifolds. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not replace or reject bundle theory; it identifies what bundle structures are the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's shadow and what Manifold forces them. When the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold reading is added, one gets both the mathematical formal machinery (Kobayashi–Nomizu 1963, Steenrod 1951, Atiyah–Bott 1983, Chamseddine–Connes–Mukhanov 2014–2015) and the physical derivation (dx₄/dt = ic). This is more, not less.

**Specific convergence: the Ehresmann horizontal/vertical decomposition and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold's spatial-vs-perpendicular-x₄-phase decomposition.** The vertical direction on a principal G-bundle corresponds to fiber-direction motion (Lie-algebra via the fundamental vector field). #### 14.19.1 The Observation That the Sphere Persists Under Wick While the Light Cone Vanishes: Status of This Fact in the Literature and Its Reading Under dx₄/dt = ic

The differential-response diagnostic of §14.18.6 rests on facts that are technically standard but were not synthesized into the framing "Wick rotation as differential-response diagnostic revealing a two-channel architecture with depth-graded content" prior to the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. Systematic literature check:

**(L-1) Metric-signature change under Wick.** The transformation of the Minkowski metric (−, +, +, +) into the Euclidean metric (+, +, +, +) is derived in every QFT textbook. Wick's original 1954 paper (G. C. Wick, *"Properties of Bethe-Salpeter Wave Functions,"* Phys. Rev. 96 (1954) 1124–1134) introduced the "rotation of the integration path in the complex plane of the [energy] variable" as a computational technique for continuing bound-state wavefunctions to complex relative-time values. The signature change is a direct consequence.

**(L-2) Poincaré group → Euclidean group.** Standard content in Streater–Wightman 1964, Glimm–Jaffe 1987, and Haag 1996 (constructive-QFT / algebraic-QFT references).

**(L-3) Light-cone destruction under Wick of curved spacetime.** M. Visser's 1991/2017 paper (M. Visser, *"How to Wick rotate generic curved spacetime,"* arXiv:1702.05572 [gr-qc], February 2017; originally 1991 Gravity Research Foundation essay) explicitly identifies the destruction of causal structure under Wick as a puzzle. Visser writes: *"After Wick rotating from Minkowski space to Euclidean space these causality constraints survive in a modified form as 'Osterwalder–Schrader positivity' (OS positivity) of the Euclidean version of the field theory. On the other hand, in the usual formulation of the transition from Lorentzian signature gravity to Euclidean signature quantum gravity the effects of the causal structure of the Lorentzian signature theory seem to disappear completely as no analogue of OS positivity is manifest. This circumstance is profoundly disturbing, and suggests that something crucial is missing in the naive analysis."* Visser's proposed remedy is to reformulate Wick rotation as a complex deformation of the spacetime metric rather than of the time coordinate.

**(L-4) Hilbert space preserved with U(t) → T(τ).** Standard content of the Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction theorem (Osterwalder–Schrader 1973 and 1975, cited at §14.18.2). Explicit in the follow-up Wightman-reconstruction literature: J. Fröhlich, K. Osterwalder, and E. Seiler, extended in D. Schlingemann, *"From Euclidean field theory to quantum field theory,"* Rev. Math. Phys. 11 (1999) 1151–1178, arXiv:hep-th/9802035, which makes explicit that the Hilbert space is the shared object between the Minkowski and Euclidean formulations, with U(t) and T(τ) being different presentations of the same underlying Hilbert-space content.

**(L-5) OS reflection positivity as the "modified causality" surviving Wick.** Visser 1991/2017 explicit again: the causality constraints *"survive in a modified form as Osterwalder–Schrader positivity."* This is precisely the identification §14.18.7 makes at the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's level, and Kontsevich–Segal 2021 (M. Kontsevich and G. Segal, *"Wick Rotation and the Positivity of Energy in Quantum Field Theory,"* Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. 72 (2021) 673, arXiv:2105.10161 [hep-th]) rigorously extended the connection between Wick rotation and the positivity of the Hamiltonian to a broader class of complex-metric contexts.

**(L-6) Woit's chirality-asymmetric formulation.** P. Woit, *"Spacetime is Right-handed,"* arXiv:2311.00608 [hep-th], submitted 1 November 2023 (revised 12 December 2023), and the March 2026 blog series expanding on the preprint (Not Even Wrong blog, "Lorentz versus Euclidean Symmetry" 4 March 2026 and successors), explicitly note the asymmetry between Minkowski and Euclidean reconstruction. Woit writes in the abstract: *"We describe the relation between vectors and spinors in complex spacetime in an unconventional chirally asymmetric manner, using purely right-handed spinors, with Minkowski spacetime getting Wick rotated to a four-dimensional Euclidean spacetime with a distinguished direction."* Woit interprets the asymmetry as a chirality signature motivating a right-handed-spacetime programme; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's interpretation is the two-channel differential-response diagnostic.

**What is not in the literature to the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's search.** The framing *"Wick preferentially destroys Algebraic-Channel-native while preserving Geometric-Channel-facing content, as a differential-response diagnostic revealing a two-channel architecture with depth-graded algebra and a Wick-covariant Geometric-Channel primitive upstream"* is not found in the searchable literature. Ivashchuk 1987–88, cited by Visser).

#### 14.19.2 Theorem 14.19.1 Under dx₄/dt = ic — Sphere Wick-Covariance vs Light-Cone Wick-Non-Invariance (Grade-1, Import): The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold Sphere Is the Primary Object, the Light Cone Is Its Coordinate Projection

*giving dx₄/dτ = +c (real rate in real Euclidean time τ). The McGucken Principle in Minkowski parametrization*

dx₄/dt = ic (14.19.2.2)

dx₄/dτ = c (14.19.2.3)

*with real rate c in real Euclidean time τ = x₄/c per Theorem 14.18.1. The Sphere's McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold is Wick-covariant.*

**Part (II) — The Manifold-tick invariants are Wick-invariant.** *The Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ, the Compton wavelength λ_C = h/(mc), and the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold-tick action ΔS = h of Theorem 14.18.2 all depend only on the Wick-invariant quantities m (rest mass, Lorentz-invariant), c (speed of light, Lorentz-invariant per SR Postulate II and derived at Theorem 2.4.5 of the Minkowski/Hilbert paper v138), and ℏ (Planck constant, Lorentz-invariant per Corollary 14.18.2.1's derivation from the Lorentz-invariance of c at the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold-tick scale). Wick rotation is a coordinate reparametrization at each event, not a Lorentz-frame change, so the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold-tick invariants persist across Wick. The Sphere retains its full McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold tick in both parametrizations.*

**Part (III) — The light cone is Wick-non-invariant.** *The Minkowski metric η with signature (−, +, +, +) transforms under Wick t → −iτ into the Euclidean metric δ with signature (+, +, +, +):*

η_{μν} = diag(−1, +1, +1, +1) ↦ δ_{μν} = diag(+1, +1, +1, +1). (14.19.2.4)

*The light cone at event p is the set of null vectors v ≠ 0 with η(v, v) = 0, forming the null hypersurface V^+(p) ∪ V^−(p) at each event. Under Wick, the null-vector equation becomes*

δ(v, v) = v₀² + v₁² + v₂² + v₃² = 0. (14.19.2.5)

*By positive-definiteness of δ, equation (14.19.2.5) has only the trivial solution v = 0. The light cone V^±(p) at each event collapses to the single point {p}. The Lorentzian causal partial order ≺ defined by V^+(p) is destroyed. *(Step a — Sphere Principle in Minkowski parametrization):* dx₄/dt = ic at every event, giving spherically symmetric expansion at rate c.

*(Step b — Coordinate squaring):* (dx₄)² = (ic dt)² = −c² dt², producing the negative sign that generates the Lorentzian signature contribution to the metric.

*(Step c — Lorentzian metric assembly):* Combining (dx₄)² = −c² dt² with the three spatial contributions dx_j² gives ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt² — the Lorentzian metric with signature (−, +, +, +) on the constraint slice 𝒞_M ⊂ ℳ_G.

*(Step d — Null hypersurface definition):* The light cone is defined as the locus of null vectors under the Lorentzian metric of Step (c).

*Under Wick rotation, Step (a) preserves physics (the Sphere persists at rate c per Part I); Step (b) flips sign under the coordinate reparametrization (dx₄)² = (c dτ)² = +c² dτ² (the negative sign of Step b in Minkowski parametrization is a consequence of the imaginary factor i in dx₄ = ic dt, which under Wick becomes the real factor giving dx₄ = c dτ); Step (c) then yields the Euclidean metric δ; Step (d) collapses the null hypersurface to a single point per Part III.*

*The upstream McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold primitive (the Sphere expansion at rate c) persists under Wick because it is a physical process; the downstream coordinate shadow (the light-cone null hypersurface) vanishes under Wick because it is a specific Lorentzian-null-hypersurface coordinate description that depends on the choice of real-time parametrization.*

#### 14.19.5 Historical Positioning of the Sphere-Wick-Persistence Under dx₄/dt = ic in the Physics Literature with Verbatim Citations: Who Noticed the Fact, Who Explained It

**(H-1) Origin of Wick rotation as computational technique.** G. C. Wick, *"Properties of Bethe-Salpeter Wave Functions,"* Phys. Rev. 96 (1954) 1124–1134, DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.96.1124. Wick's original paper introduced the "rotation of the integration path in the complex plane of the [energy] variable" as a mathematical technique for computing bound-state wavefunctions of two-body systems in relativistic quantum field theory. The abstract states: *"A boundary condition at t = ±∞ (t being the 'relative' time variable) is obtained for the four-dimensional wave function of a two-body system in a bound state. It is shown that this condition implies that the wave function can be continued analytically to complex values of the 'relative time' variable;... a wave equation satisfied by this function is obtained by rotation of the integration path in the complex plane of the variable [p_0], and it is further shown that the formulation of the eigenvalue problem in terms of this equation presents several advantages in that many of the ordinary mathematical methods become available."* Wick presented the rotation as a computational device; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's Manifold-coordinate reading τ = x₄/c is the physical interpretation absent from Wick's original.
