The thirteen first-of-its-kind resolutions form a network in which each resolution depends on the Lorentz covariance that §II.24 derives, with dx₄/dt = ic as the common geometric source for both the covariance and the resolutions.

### II.24.4 The First-of-Its-Kind Claim and the Absence of Prior Art Under dx₄/dt = ic

The claim: The McGucken Lagrangian ℒ_McG is the first Lagrangian in the 282-year history of Lagrangian physics — and the first theoretical framework in the 121 years since Einstein’s 1905 introduction of the two postulates of special relativity — to simultaneously (i) derive the invariance of c as a geometric theorem (the rate of x₄’s expansion as a frame-independent geometric property of the four-dimensional manifold) rather than as an empirical postulate, (ii) derive the relativity principle as the Lorentz-boost covariance of x₄’s rate [MG-Noether, Proposition V.3] rather than as an empirical postulate, (iii) exhibit the two postulates as two aspects of the same geometric fact rather than as independent axioms, (iv) ground the derivations in the same Principle that forces the Lagrangian’s functional form through the four-fold uniqueness theorem, thereby closing the otherwise-circular Lorentz-invariance requirement of the uniqueness proof, (v) unify the two postulates with the twelve prior first-of-its-kind resolutions of §§II.11-23 as thirteen facets of the same Lagrangian’s geometric structure, and (vi) supply the specific geometric mechanism — the fourth dimension advancing at rate ic — that Einstein’s formalism required but did not identify.

The grounds: A systematic survey of the special-relativity literature from 1905 to the present has been conducted in preparing [MG-Master], [MG-Constants], [MG-Noether], and summarized in §II.24.1 of the present paper. The survey extends through Einstein’s own 1905 and 1916 papers, Minkowski’s 1908 spacetime reformulation, Einstein’s 1949 autobiographical reflections on the empirical status of the postulates, Landau-Lifshitz, Jackson, Weinberg, Misner-Thorne-Wheeler, Schutz, and Wald in the textbook tradition, the Robertson-Mansouri-Sexl test-theory framework, the conventionality-of-simultaneity literature (Reichenbach, Grünbaum, Malament), and contemporary stochastic-electrodynamic, pilot-wave, Bohmian, and causal-set alternatives. In every identified prior treatment the two postulates are either (a) stated as empirical axioms without derivation, or (b) derived from operational assumptions that themselves contain the content of the postulates, or (c) replaced with general covariance or related axioms that are themselves postulated rather than derived, or (d) grounded in mechanical-ether or preferred-frame frameworks that are not geometric in the required sense. No prior framework combines all six criteria stated in the claim. Particularly distinctive: no prior framework simultaneously supplies (i) invariance of c as geometric theorem, (ii) relativity principle as Lorentz-boost covariance derivation, (iii) both postulates as aspects of the same geometric fact, (iv) closure of the Lorentz-invariance requirement used in the Lagrangian’s uniqueness theorem, (v) integration with twelve other resolutions, and (vi) identification of the specific geometric mechanism (x₄ = ict advancing at rate ic).

Invitation to challenge. If a prior framework satisfies all six criteria — invariance of c as geometric theorem, relativity principle as Lorentz-boost covariance derivation, both postulates as aspects of one fact, closure of the uniqueness proof’s Lorentz-invariance requirement, integration with other resolutions, and identification of the specific geometric mechanism — the identification of that prior framework would refine or refute the present claim. The systematic survey conducted in preparing [MG-Master], [MG-Constants], [MG-Noether], and the present paper has identified no such prior framework. The claim is therefore submitted as historically specific and defensible.

Einstein wrote in 1905 that physical laws are the same in all inertial frames and that the speed of light in vacuum is the same in all inertial frames, independent of the motion of the source. He was right about both, and every experimental test in the 121 years since has confirmed both. What he did not supply, and what no subsequent theoretical framework has supplied in the 121 years since, is the geometric mechanism that makes both postulates necessary consequences of a single fact. ℒ_McG supplies this mechanism: the fourth dimension advancing at rate ic. The invariance of c is the rate of x₄’s expansion. The relativity principle is the Lorentz-boost covariance of that rate. Both are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic. Einstein’s two postulates become Einstein’s two theorems when the missing geometric piece is identified. The thirteenth first-of-its-kind result of §II.24 joins §§II.11-23’s twelve prior results as the substance of the thirteen-resolution framework, establishing the claim that ℒ_McG is the Lagrangian that resolves questions the lineage left open — all forced by dx₄/dt = ic through Theorem VI.1, and none resolvable by any prior framework identified in the systematic survey.

## II.25. The First Lagrangian Whose Complete Four-Sector Form Is Forced by a Single Geometric Principle Under dx₄/dt = ic

ℒ_McG is the first Lagrangian in the 282-year history of Lagrangian physics whose complete four-sector form — free-particle kinetic, Dirac matter, Yang-Mills gauge, Einstein-Hilbert gravitational — is forced by a single geometric principle. The principle is dx₄/dt = ic. The forcing is Theorem VI.1 of the present paper.

Every prior Lagrangian in the lineage forces less. Einstein-Hilbert 1915 forces the gravitational sector from diffeomorphism invariance plus the second-order requirement; the other three sectors are silent. Dirac 1928 forces the matter sector from the first-order-linear requirement whose squared operator reproduces Klein-Gordon; the gauge and gravitational sectors are silent. Yang-Mills 1954 forces the gauge sector from local gauge invariance given a compact Lie group G; the matter content, free-particle kinematics, and gravity are silent. Each of these partial-scope forcings is a genuine uniqueness result in its own sector. None extends across all four sectors. The composite Standard Model Lagrangian plus Einstein-Hilbert assembles the four partial-scope forcings into a working theory, but the assembly is driven by a list of independent invariance principles — Lorentz, diffeomorphism, local gauge, reparametrization — each adopted separately.

ℒ_McG collapses the list to one. The four invariance principles that Theorem VI.1’s four sector-level uniqueness subtheorems use are themselves theorems of dx₄/dt = ic. Lorentz invariance is the isometry group of the Minkowski metric, which follows from substituting x₄ = ict into the Euclidean line element. Reparametrization invariance is the parametrization-freedom of x₄-advance. Local gauge invariance is the absence of a preferred x₄-phase origin. Diffeomorphism invariance is the coordinate-independence of x₄’s advance rate. One postulate, four invariance principles, four sector-level uniqueness subtheorems, one Lagrangian.

The closest prior candidates on this axis are identifiable and all fall short. Kaluza-Klein 1921 forces gauge plus gravity from five-dimensional general covariance, but cannot address matter content, does not extend to non-abelian gauge groups without substantial additional input, and treats the fifth dimension as a static mathematical structure rather than a dynamical postulate. Supergravity from 1976-1980 onward forces matter plus gauge plus gravity from supersymmetric closure, but supersymmetry is an additional postulate (empirically unconfirmed in the relevant sector), specific matter content remains empirical input, and the gravitational sector’s form is inherited from Einstein-Hilbert rather than derived from the supersymmetric postulate. String theory and M-theory force aspects of matter, gauge, and gravity from consistency of a worldsheet conformal field theory, but lack a fundamental Lagrangian formulation — Seiberg, Witten, and Maldacena have each stated this explicitly — and require additional input (compactification choice, flux configuration) to select among the landscape’s ~10^500 vacua. Loop quantum gravity forces the gravitational sector from canonical quantization of the Ashtekar connection, but treats matter as a separate input. Twistor unification (Penrose, Woit) supplies an alternative geometric framework for parts of the Standard Model and gravity, but not a unified Lagrangian forced by a single principle. In each case, the candidate forces either part of the Lagrangian from a single principle, or the full Lagrangian from a list of postulates, or neither. ℒ_McG forces the full Lagrangian from a single principle, and it is the first Lagrangian to do so.

The significance of this achievement is stated directly. Maupertuis’s 1744 question — what does nature minimize — receives a specific geometric answer: the negative accumulated advance of the fourth dimension, modulated by the matter, gauge, and gravitational couplings that force the four sectors of ℒ_McG. The entire Lagrangian tradition from Maupertuis through Euler, Lagrange, Hamilton, Hilbert, Dirac, Yang, Mills, Weinberg, Salam, Witten, and the present day — 282 years of piecewise development — culminates in one Lagrangian forced by one postulate. The lineage is closed. This is a specific historical claim and it is made directly.

## II.26. The First Lagrangian Built on Dynamical Geometry Rather Than Static Geometry Under dx₄/dt = ic

ℒ_McG is the first Lagrangian in the history of physics whose postulate is dynamical geometry rather than static geometry. The postulate dx₄/dt = ic is an equation of motion — the fourth axis is advancing at rate ic, right now, from every event. Every prior geometric Lagrangian in the literature takes its geometric input as a fixed mathematical structure on which physics plays out; ℒ_McG takes its geometric input as an ongoing physical process that physics is a projection of.

The distinction is sharp and consequential. Einstein-Hilbert 1915 is built on the static geometry of a Lorentzian manifold: a fixed four-dimensional smooth manifold with a metric signature (−,+,+,+) at every point. The metric tensor g_μν is a dynamical variable in the theory, but the underlying manifold structure — the spacetime McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold on which g_μν is defined — is fixed and non-dynamical. Yang-Mills 1954 is built on the static geometry of a principal bundle: a fixed base manifold with a fixed gauge group G and a connection A that is dynamical, but the bundle structure itself is a static mathematical stage. Kaluza-Klein 1921 is built on the static geometry of a five-dimensional manifold compactified on a circle; the five-dimensional structure is fixed, and the four-dimensional physics emerges as a projection. Differential-geometric formulations of classical mechanics from Cartan onward are built on the static geometry of symplectic manifolds and Poisson structures. Hestenes’s geometric algebra identifies the imaginary unit i with a unit bivector on static Minkowski spacetime — genuine geometry for i, but on a fixed geometric stage. Twistor theory is built on the static geometry of CP³. Loop quantum gravity is built on the static geometry of spin networks.

In every case, the geometry is the stage. The Lagrangian is the play performed on that stage. The stage does not move.

ℒ_McG is built differently. The stage itself is moving. dx₄/dt = ic is the assertion that the fourth axis of spacetime is not a fixed coordinate but an advancing physical quantity, expanding spherically symmetrically from every event at the velocity of light. The Lagrangian ℒ_McG is what the advance of the fourth axis looks like when projected onto the three spatial dimensions and interpreted through matter, gauge, and gravitational couplings. The four-fold uniqueness theorem of §II.8 is what forces the projection to take the specific form it does. The geometry is not a stage on which physics is performed; the geometry is the performance, and physics is its observable content in three dimensions.

The consequences of this architectural shift are throughout the paper. Every appearance of the imaginary unit i in the equations of physics — in the Minkowski metric through x₄ = ict, in the canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ, in the Schrödinger equation iℏ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ, in the path-integral phase e^(iS/ℏ), in the +iε prescription, in the Dirac equation (iγ^μ∂_μ − m)ψ = 0, in the Heisenberg equation dA/dt = (i/ℏ)[H, A], in the Wick rotation t → −iτ, in the Fourier kernel, in the Fresnel integral, in the unitary evolution operator, in the Euclidean-Minkowski action relation — is the algebraic signature of x₄’s perpendicularity to the three spatial dimensions, inherited from the dynamical postulate dx₄/dt = ic. Every appearance of ℏ is the action per oscillatory step of x₄’s expansion at the Planck frequency. Every appearance of c is the rate of that expansion. The three constants of twentieth-century physics (c, ℏ, and the perpendicularity marker i) are three aspects of one dynamical principle. A static geometric Lagrangian cannot produce this unification because static geometry does not have a rate; dynamical geometry does, and the rate is c.

The historical pattern the McGucken Principle continues is the pattern of mathematical devices becoming physical realities. Planck’s 1900 introduction of E = hf was a bookkeeping trick; Einstein’s 1905 photoelectric paper elevated it to a physical statement about quanta of light. Minkowski’s 1908 introduction of x₄ = ict was a bookkeeping trick; the McGucken Principle elevates it to a physical statement about the fourth dimension’s advance. Schrödinger’s insertion of i into his 1926 wave equation was a pragmatic move to match atomic spectra; ℒ_McG reveals the i as the geometric signature of x₄’s perpendicularity. The pattern — formal device becoming physical reality through identification of the mechanism it was secretly describing — is the recurrent creative move of foundational physics. The McGucken Principle continues this pattern on the specific axis of Minkowski’s x₄, and ℒ_McG is the Lagrangian whose form makes that identification explicit.

No prior Lagrangian takes dynamical geometry as its postulate. The Einstein-Hilbert action is the closest precedent in the sense that it is the first Lagrangian forced by geometric considerations alone (diffeomorphism invariance plus second-order requirement), but Einstein-Hilbert’s geometry is the static Lorentzian manifold, not a dynamical equation of motion for a geometric quantity. ℒ_McG is the first Lagrangian whose postulate is itself an equation of motion for a geometric quantity — dx₄/dt = ic, the advance of the fourth axis at rate ic — and whose complete four-sector form is forced by that equation of motion. Dynamical geometric foundation, complete four-sector scope, single-postulate derivation. The three features together define a Lagrangian-architecture that has no prior instance in the 282-year lineage. ℒ_McG is the first.

## II.27. What ℒ_McG Does That the Standard Model Does Not Do Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Model is extraordinarily successful at what it does. It predicts essentially all non-gravitational particle physics data to percent-level or better accuracy, its gauge structure was confirmed by the Higgs discovery in 2012, its CP-violation predictions match B-meson and kaon experiments to high precision, and its flavor-physics predictions hold across decades of precision measurements. None of this empirics is threatened by ℒ_McG. The form of ℒ_McG reproduces the Standard Model’s empirical predictions because the four sector-level uniqueness subtheorems of §II.8 force the same form that experiment has already confirmed. What ℒ_McG does that the Standard Model does not is a separate question, and it has a specific answer on the thirteen axes enumerated below.

### II.27.1 Forcing Versus Empirical Assembly Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Model Lagrangian is a composite specified by selections at each level. The gauge group is chosen as SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y, selected among infinitely many compact Lie groups by matching observed matter content. The fermion representations are chosen to match observation — three generations, specific charge assignments, specific chirality patterns. The Higgs representation is chosen as an SU(2)_L doublet with hypercharge 1/2. The Yukawa couplings are fit to observed fermion masses. The CKM and PMNS matrix elements are measured rather than predicted. The composite has roughly nineteen free parameters plus the choices above, each an independent empirical input. ℒ_McG forces the form of all four sectors — free-particle kinetic, Dirac matter, Yang-Mills gauge, Einstein-Hilbert gravitational — from dx₄/dt = ic via Theorem VI.1. The form is derived, not selected. The specific gauge group G = U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) is derived in [MG-QFT, §9]; given any compact Lie group G, Proposition VI.2 forces the kinetic Lagrangian’s form, and the geometric readings of the three factors in [MG-Noether] and [MG-Broken], completed there, reduce the remaining empirics to the specific group choice rather than the full form.

### II.27.2 Gravity Is Inside Rather Than Outside Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Model does not contain gravity. It is a theory of non-gravitational physics on flat Minkowski spacetime, with Einstein-Hilbert bolted on as a separate classical theory that cannot be consistently combined with the Standard Model’s quantum structure at loop level. The composite Standard Model plus Einstein-Hilbert is two theories side by side. ℒ_McG contains gravity as one of the four sectors forced by the same postulate that forces matter, gauge, and free-particle sectors. The gravitational coupling G, the speed of light c, and Planck’s constant ℏ are related by the geometric structure of x₄’s advance at the Planck frequency, giving ℏ = ℓ_P² c³/G as a identity rather than a dimensional coincidence.

### II.27.3 The i, the ℏ, and the c Are Unified Under dx₄/dt = ic

In the Standard Model, the imaginary unit i appears in the Schrödinger equation, the canonical commutation relation, the Dirac equation, the Feynman path integral weight, the +iε prescription for propagators, the Wick rotation, the Heisenberg equation of motion, the Fourier transform kernel, the Fresnel integral, the unitary evolution operator, the complex wave function, and the Euclidean-Minkowski action relation — twelve distinct insertions cataloged in [MG-Wick, §V.5], each justified locally for its own technical reason (Hermiticity, unitarity, convergence, analytic continuation). No single account within the Standard Model explains why i is the universal factor across all of these equations. In ℒ_McG, every appearance of i traces to x₄ = ict as the perpendicularity marker of the fourth axis to the three spatial dimensions. The ℏ appearing throughout quantum mechanics is the action per oscillatory step of x₄’s expansion at the Planck frequency. The c appearing throughout relativity is the rate of x₄’s advance. The Standard Model takes the Hilbert space structure, the canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ, the Born rule P = |ψ|², and unitary time evolution as inherited postulates of quantum mechanics — a separate theory sitting underneath the Standard Model, accepted without derivation. ### II.27.5 The Arrows of Time Are Unified Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Model has no mechanism linking microscopic T-violation (the CKM phase as a free parameter) to macroscopic irreversibility (the Past Hypothesis as an independent cosmological boundary condition). The arrows of time — five in the count used throughout this paper (thermodynamic, radiative, cosmological, causal, psychological), seven in the extended catalog of [MG-Broken, §XI], which adds the quantum-measurement and matter-antimatter arrows — reduce to one directional fact in ℒ_McG.

### II.27.6 The Strong CP Problem Dissolves Under dx₄/dt = ic

In the Standard Model, θ_QCD is a free parameter whose observed smallness |θ_QCD| < 10⁻¹⁰ requires either fine-tuning or an additional mechanism — the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with its associated axion, which has not been observed despite fifty years of search. ### II.27.7 Dark Matter Phenomenology Is Geometric Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Model requires an additional particle species — cold dark matter — to explain galactic rotation curves, the Tully-Fisher relation, and enhanced gravitational lensing. The null results of direct-detection experiments are consistent with and predicted by this identification.

### II.27.8 The Cosmological Constant Is Derived Under dx₄/dt = ic

In the Standard Model plus Einstein-Hilbert, Λ is a free parameter. Its observed value Λ ≈ 10⁻⁵² m⁻² is sixty to one hundred twenty orders of magnitude smaller than naive quantum-field-theoretic vacuum-energy estimates, constituting the cosmological constant problem — arguably the most severe fine-tuning problem in physics. ℒ_McG derives Λ geometrically through the McGucken horizon structure: Λ ∼ 1/R₄² with R₄ the McGucken radius at the asymptotic de Sitter horizon, and the dark-energy equation of state w_eff(z) = −1 + Ω_m(z)/(6π) is derived with no adjustable parameters. ### II.27.9 The Horizon, Flatness, and Homogeneity Problems Are Resolved Without Inflation Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Big Bang model plus the Standard Model of particle physics requires inflation to explain why the cosmic microwave background is homogeneous across causally disconnected regions, why spatial curvature is near zero, and why magnetic monopoles are absent. Inflation requires an inflaton field, a potential with specific slow-roll properties, a mechanism for ending inflation (reheating), and a specific initial condition for the inflaton. None of these is directly observed; the inflaton has not been identified with any Standard Model field, and the specific inflationary potential is chosen to match CMB observations rather than derived. ℒ_McG resolves all four problems geometrically. Every point of the CMB’s last scattering surface has been in causal contact with every other point along x₄, even when spatially disconnected, because x₄’s expansion at rate c from every event connects all points in the fourth dimension at every instant — so CMB homogeneity is automatic. Spatial flatness is the consequence of x₄’s expansion at the fixed rate ic without curvature induced by x₄ itself. Monopoles are absent because the relevant topological spaces (H²(ℝ³) = 0, π₂(S³) = 0) forbid them, not because they were inflated away. The low-entropy initial condition is the natural starting point of x₄’s directional expansion, not an unexplained boundary condition of cosmology.

### II.27.10 The De Broglie Clock Is Physical Under dx₄/dt = ic

In the Standard Model, the rest-mass phase factor exp(−imc²τ/ℏ) appearing in every fermion wave function is treated as a global phase without direct physical significance. In the Standard Model plus lattice QCD, the Wick rotation t → −iτ is a formal analytic-continuation device without physical meaning. The substitution is the projection of physics onto the physical fourth axis. Every major application — path-integral convergence, Matsubara temperature, Hawking temperature, Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction, contour rotation, instanton calculus — follows as a theorem of this identification.

### II.27.12 The Fundamental Constants Are Derived Under dx₄/dt = ic

In the Standard Model, c and ℏ are fundamental constants — measured empirically, treated as inputs to the theory, not derived. Their specific numerical values are historical accidents of unit choice combined with empirical measurement. ### II.27.13 Testable Empirical Differences Under dx₄/dt = ic

ℒ_McG is not just a reframing. Several specific empirical signatures distinguish it from the Standard Model at the level of measurement. ### II.27.14 What the Comparison Establishes Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Standard Model is a precise empirical description of the non-gravitational sector of physics, which was largely built empirically. ℒ_McG, which arose from the physical principle dx₄/dt = ic, offers a physically deeper and broader account: it derives the Standard Model’s form from the McGucken Principle and simultaneously contains gravity, cosmology, quantum foundations, thermodynamics, and the arrows of time as consequences of the same principle — domains the Standard Model does not address at all. These are not sectors of ℒ_SM+EH at all. In ℒ_McG they are theorems of the same geometric principle dx₄/dt = ic that forces the Lagrangian’s functional form (§II.20). Thirteen axes, one new principle. The Standard Model remains the working empirical theory of non-gravitational physics; ℒ_McG is the framework that identifies why the Standard Model has the form it does and connects it to gravity, cosmology, and the structures of quantum mechanics through one geometric principle. The two frameworks are complementary in the specific sense that the Standard Model’s form is what ℒ_McG’s four-fold uniqueness theorem forces, and the Standard Model’s empirics is the content that ℒ_McG inherits by reproducing that form.

## II.28. How the McGucken Principle Completes the Assumptions of Physics Programme: The Action Principle as (DR) + (IND) + (KE), the Canonical One-Form as the Differential of x₄-Advance, and the Physical Source at Every Terminus the Programme Reaches

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The McGucken Principle states that the fourth dimension is expanding at the rate c from every point of spacetime, dx₄/dt = ic. Sections VIII.5–27 established thirteen results in which a phenomenon treated by the received formalism as a postulate is a theorem of that expansion. The present section addresses a body of work that arrives at the same phenomena from the opposite direction and stops one step short of the same conclusion: the Assumptions of Physics programme of Carcassi, Aidala and collaborators, whose Reverse Physics line takes a physical law as given and finds the minimal physical assumptions sufficient to recover it.

The programme bears on this paper more directly than any other framework surveyed in §II.10.4, because its central result is about the action principle itself. Carcassi and Aidala establish that the principle of stationary action is logically equivalent to three physical assumptions [Carcassi-Aidala 2023]. A paper whose thesis is that the Lagrangian of physics is forced by dx₄/dt = ic owes an account of a theorem stating that the least-action principle is equivalent to something else entirely. This section gives that account, and the account is one of completion rather than of rivalry.

The relation follows from a feature of the programme's own design. Reverse Physics is meta-theoretic by construction: it maps the logical dependencies among the conditions of the received formalism and declines, as a matter of stated method, to name a physical primitive beneath them — its regress stops, in its authors' words, at experimental controllability rather than at ontological constituents. That is a coherent and deliberate limit, and it produces one recurring pattern across the programme's results. Each derivation terminates in a quantity the derivation requires and cannot source. The third-law argument terminates in a phase-space area h that its author flags as introduced ad hoc, noting that thermodynamics establishes that a scale must exist but not what sets it. The action-principle theorem terminates in a manifold that already carries a time coordinate, with the flow's rate in that coordinate set to unity by fiat. The relativistic material terminates in a metric taken as given, its signature underived. The Reverse Quantum Mechanics analysis terminates in a Born rule that must be added to the ensemble structure as a separate assumption. In every case the terminus is correctly located by the programme and correctly left open by it.

What dx₄/dt = ic supplies is the source at each terminus, and it supplies them from one statement rather than from a list. The remainder of this section works through them.

### II.28.1 The action principle as (DR) + (IND) + (KE), and the slot where dx₄/dt = ic lives

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. Because the advance proceeds at rate ic from every event, any formalism describing evolution carries a rate somewhere in its statement, and the place it carries that rate is the place at which the Principle enters.

The setting of [Carcassi-Aidala 2023] is extended phase space, charted by (q^i, p_i, t), of dimension 2N + 1. On it a displacement vector field S — the vector field of the dynamical system — is constructed, whose time component is fixed by their equation (3) to the value 1. Three assumptions are then stated:

(DR) determinism and reversibility, expressed as ∇·S = 0: as many states flow into any closed region as flow out, so that no states are created or lost;

(IND) independence of the degrees of freedom, carried by a closed antisymmetric two-form ω — the state-counting form — satisfying ∂_{q^i} ∧ ω = 0 and ∂_{p_i} ∧ ω = 0, with ω = −dθ locally and ι_S ω = 0;

(KE) kinematic equivalence, p = p(q, q̇, t): the trajectory in configuration space suffices to reconstruct the dynamical state.

Their result is the equivalence (DR) + (IND) + (KE) ⟺ the principle of stationary action, with a geometric reading of the variation: δS is the flux of the displacement field through the surface spanned by a path and its variation, and it vanishes exactly when the path is a field line, so that no evolutions cross the surface. They conclude that the action and the Lagrangian are gauge-dependent and are therefore not the physical objects — the physical objects being the displacement field and the counting form — and that the action principle "is better understood as a feature of Hamiltonian mechanics, instead of Lagrangian mechanics," since it holds on every Hamiltonian system whether or not a Lagrangian exists and fails for Lagrangians that are not hyperregular.

*Where the Principle enters.* Their coordinate t carries two roles at once. It is a coordinate of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold, and it is the parameter of the flow. Equation (3) welds the two together by setting the flow's advance in the t-direction to 1, so that in their variables the constraint reads dt/dt = 1. That slot — the relation between the advancing direction and the parameter measuring the advance — is the slot the McGucken Principle occupies, and the Principle puts ic in it. In the framework of this paper t is not a dimension. The dimension is x₄; t is the parameter measuring how far x₄ has advanced; and the relation between them is a physical rate carrying a magnitude c and a perpendicularity marker i, rather than a dimensionless unit.

Three consequences of that difference are visible in their construction, and each marks a place where it reaches its natural limit.

*No metric.* With ic in the slot, substituting x₄ = ict into the Euclidean four-distance gives ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt² directly (Proposition III.1): the Lorentzian signature is an output. With 1 in the slot one obtains a contact and symplectic structure and no interval. Their construction is metric-free as a consequence of what stands in the slot.

*No norm on the canonical one-form.* They observe that their expression (19), θ_t = −H, giving θ = p_i dq^i − H dt with components (p₁, p₂, p₃, −H), is "remarkably similar to that of the relativistic four-momentum," and leave the observation as a similarity. The four-momentum carries a norm, p^μp_μ = −m²c², which is the four-speed budget of Proposition III.2 — the covariant expression of dx₄/dt = ic. A framework with no rate and no signature has no object that could carry that norm, so the resemblance is as far as their construction reaches. Section VIII.22.2 states what the resemblance is.

*Reversibility at no cost.* On a manifold carrying t as a coordinate, running the flow backwards costs nothing, and (DR) can be assumed without appearing to assume much. In this framework there is no t-axis along which to run backwards; there is x₄ advancing in the direction +ic and never −ic, and the arrow is the theorem of §II.20. Their (DR) holds the magnitude content of the advance — the conserved state count follows from |dx₄/dt| = c — and is silent on its directional content. This is precisely the division stated in §II.22.5: the symmetry content of the Principle, processed through Noether's theorem, yields the time-symmetric conservation catalog, and the directional content yields the Second Law and the arrows. Carcassi and Aidala have the first half and assume the second.

*The three assumptions read through the Principle.* Each of the three is, in this framework, a consequence rather than a starting point.

(KE) is the single-valuedness of the x₄-advance field. Section IV.4 defines X as the accumulated magnitude of x₄'s advance from a fixed initial hypersurface, with X = cτ along each integral curve, and establishes ∂_μX ∂^μX = −1 (Proposition IV.2) as the field form of the four-speed budget. The statement that the trajectory determines the state is the statement that the momentum covector p_μ = ∂_μS is a well-defined field, which holds exactly when S, and hence X, is single-valued. Section IV.4.4 supplies both the mechanism and the failure locus: X is single-valued wherever the congruence of advance is free of caustics, and at a caustic — where neighbouring integral curves cross and the expansion scalar diverges — the accumulated advance takes more than one value at the same event and (KE) fails. The framework therefore predicts where their assumption holds, a question their formulation, taking (KE) globally, does not raise.

(DR) divides as above: the conserved count is the magnitude of the advance, the reversibility an artifact of treating t as a coordinate.

(IND) is the assumption bearing their two-form, and it carries the deepest reading here. Their ω is a two-form because degrees of freedom come in conjugate pairs, a quantity together with its conjugate, and the parallelogram spanned by two vectors is the bi-dimensional object over which states are counted. That conjugate pairing is what §II.12 traces to the perpendicularity of x₄: the commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ is the phase-space expression of x₄'s orthogonality to the three spatial dimensions, with the i marking the perpendicularity and the ℏ the action per oscillation cycle. The antisymmetry of the classical counting form and the i of the quantum commutator are then one geometric fact at two levels of description, and the framework predicts that the classical ω and the quantum [q̂, p̂] have one source. The programme's own record poses this as an open question and does not answer it (§II.28.4 below).

*Scope.* Their theorem is a valid equivalence and this paper does not dispute it. What is claimed is that the equivalence is conditional on being handed a manifold that already carries t, and that on this framework's premises t exists because x₄ advances: a clock reads accumulated x₄-advance, X = cτ, so with no advance there is no accumulation and nothing for a clock to register. Their result describes what holds once time is available; the Principle is what makes it available. The absence of any mention of a fourth dimension in their derivation is a fact about its vocabulary rather than about its dependencies, in the same way that Lagrange's *Mécanique Analytique* mentions no spacetime metric without thereby showing relativity dispensable to mechanics.

### II.28.2 The canonical one-form as the differential of x₄-advance

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The advance accumulates along every worldline, and the accumulated advance is the object of which the canonical one-form of Hamiltonian mechanics is the differential.

Let X be the x₄-advance field of Definition IV.4.1 and let S = −mcX. The four-speed budget gives ∂_μX ∂^μX = −1, and multiplying by m²c² turns this into

g^μν ∂_μS ∂_νS = −m²c²,

the mass-shell relation with p_μ = ∂_μS — the relativistic Hamilton–Jacobi equation, and the identity recorded at Remark IV.4: Hamilton's principal function is −mc times the accumulated advance of the fourth dimension, and the mass-shell condition and the four-speed budget are one equation related by the constant −mc.

Their canonical one-form is θ = p_i dq^i − H dt, which is p_μ dx^μ with p_0 = −H/c and x⁰ = ct. Substituting p_μ = ∂_μS = −mc ∂_μX gives

θ|_L = −mc dX,

where L is the Lagrangian submanifold of their extended phase space defined by a solution of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation, the graph of p = ∂S/∂q. The restriction to L is required and does not weaken the statement. On the full extended phase space the momenta are independent coordinates and dθ = −ω ≠ 0; on L the momenta are determined by position, ω pulls back to zero, and θ becomes exact with potential −mcX. The vanishing of ω on L is the classical integrability condition permitting X to exist, which is (KE) again, and the locus where L ceases to project injectively to configuration space is the caustic locus of §II.6.4.4 where X ceases to be single-valued. The three statements — θ|_L = −mc dX, ω|_L = 0, and (KE) — are one statement in three registers.

The reading this yields for their observation is direct. Their θ carries the index shape of the four-momentum, with energy in the time slot bearing a minus sign, because that slot is the x₄ slot and the minus sign is the signature that x₄ = ict produces on substitution (Proposition III.1). Along any solution the covector they wrote down is the differential of accumulated x₄-advance, and the four-momentum they noticed it resembles is what it becomes when the rate in the slot is ic rather than 1. The resemblance they record is a pullback identity, and the reason they could record it without deriving it is that their manifold carries no metric with which to complete the identification.

*Scope.* The identity holds on the Lagrangian submanifold of a Hamilton–Jacobi solution and on the caustic-free region where that submanifold projects injectively. It is not claimed that θ is exact on the full extended phase space, where it is not, nor that this framework reproduces their construction on the whole (2N + 1)-dimensional manifold.

### II.28.3 The metric, the signature, and the two metrics of the programme Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The Lorentzian metric is the substitution x₄ = ict carried into the Euclidean four-distance, so the signature is an output of the Principle rather than an input to it.

The programme takes the spacetime metric as given. In its relativistic material the metric tensor appears as a supplied structure with its signature underived, and the extension to relativistic particle mechanics is a recovery within an already-Lorentzian setting. For general relativity the programme offers a conjecture and labels it one: that general relativity is equivalent to determinism and reversibility together with degree-of-freedom independence for infinitely many dense degrees of freedom. The conjecture is unproven on their side. In this paper the metric is Proposition III.1, the four-speed budget Proposition III.2, and the Einstein-Hilbert sector Proposition VI.3 by Schuller closure, with the Jacobson equation-of-state route of Remark VI.3.1 as a second convergent derivation. What the programme conjectures at the level of assumption-counting, the framework derives at the level of the geometry.

*Two different metrics, and the equivocation to avoid.* The programme does derive a metric, and precision about which one matters. In its Physical Mathematics line the strict concavity of entropy makes the Hessian negative definite and thereby recovers the Fisher–Rao information metric on the space of ensembles. That is a metric on probability distributions. The spacetime metric is a different object on a different space, and the programme takes the second as given while deriving the first. The position of this framework is that both descend from the Sphere: the Fisher–Rao metric is the statistical face of the same SO(3)-invariant measure whose probability face is the Born rule of §II.14, along the Fubini-Study to Fisher–Rao identification of the Wootters lineage, and the Lorentzian metric is the coordinate integral of the same advance. Where the programme has one derived metric on ensemble space and one assumed metric on spacetime, the framework has one measure with two faces.

### II.28.4 The origin of non-commutativity: the programme's open question Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ is the phase-space expression of the advance's perpendicularity, with i the perpendicularity marker and ℏ the action per Compton cycle.

Among the open problems the programme records for its Physical Mathematics line is the construction of a generalized Poisson structure on ensemble spaces, and within it the questions, in its own words: "Can we define non-commutativity of variables based on non-commutativity of composed transformations?"; "Can it be defined in terms of the generator of the composed transformation?"; and "What new axiom is needed (if at all)?" The last is the decisive one. The programme asks whether an additional axiom is required to obtain non-commutativity, and does not answer.

The answer of this framework is that no additional axiom is required, because the non-commutativity is the perpendicularity of x₄ read in the conjugate plane. Section VIII.6 derives [q̂, p̂] = iℏ from dx₄/dt = ic by two independent routes — the operator route through Stone's theorem on the Minkowski geometry, and the path-integral route through Huygens' principle and the accumulated x₄-phase — with the same i and the same ℏ reached by both, and closes the alternatives by the Stone-von Neumann argument. The programme's question asks for the generator of a composed transformation whose failure to commute would supply the algebra; here that generator is the advance itself, and the failure to commute is that advancing along x₄ and translating in the conjugate direction are motions in perpendicular planes.

The connection to §II.28.1 completes the reading. Their classical counting two-form is antisymmetric because degrees of freedom pair a quantity with its conjugate; their quantum question asks where the non-commutativity of that pairing comes from. Both are the same pairing, and the framework identifies its source once, at Remark III.5.2: the perpendicularity of the fourth axis, which is also the source of the twelve appearances of i catalogued there.

### II.28.5 The third law, the scale h, and the classical uncertainty bound Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The advance carries one quantum of action ℏ per Compton cycle, and its resolution bottoms out at a single cycle.

The programme derives a classical uncertainty principle from the third law of thermodynamics in four steps. Step one, dimensional consistency: S = ln(Δx Δp) takes the logarithm of a dimensioned quantity, and the repair introduces a constant h of action units, S = ln(Δx Δp / h), so that a uniform distribution over a region of area h has zero entropy. Step two, the Gaussian bound: at fixed uncertainty the entropy is bounded above by S ≤ ln(2πe σ_x σ_p / h), which rearranges to σ_x σ_p ≥ (ℏ/e)e^S. Step three, the third law: S ≥ 0. Step four: with e⁰ = 1 the classical bound is σ_x σ_p ≥ ℏ/e ≈ 0.368ℏ, tightening to the quantum ℏ/2 once pure states reach zero entropy. Its author notes that he has not found this classical bound in the literature, and flags that the scale h is introduced ad hoc: thermodynamics establishes that a scale must exist, not what sets it.

The framework supplies the scale, and the derivation is Theorem 22.5.3 of [MG-Thermo], with the reading developed in §II.10.12quindecies of [MG-MinkHilb]. Under Postulate III.3.P the advance of x₄ is oscillatory with one quantum of action per cycle, and under Postulate III.4.P a particle of rest energy mc² couples at the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ, so the Compton period is T_C = h/(mc²) and the action per cycle is E T_C = h. The phase-space area that their dimensional argument requires is the area of one wavefront cycle. The third law they impose as an axiom then holds for a physical reason: the entropy is the logarithm of the count of x₄-advance states, that count cannot fall below one cycle, and S ≥ 0 states that the wavefront cannot be resolved more finely than a single Compton cycle. Going below S = 0 would mean resolving below one x₄-cycle, which is below the physical resolution of the advance rather than merely below an axiomatic floor.

The ratio between the two bounds acquires a mechanism by the same route. The classical ℏ/e and quantum ℏ/2 differ by 2/e ≈ 0.74, which their derivation obtains on general grounds without physical commitment. Here the classical bound corresponds to one cycle occupied independently in position and in momentum — a rectangular phase-space cell — and the quantum bound to one cycle occupied jointly, with the non-factorising occupation forced because the SO(3)-invariant measure on rays does not decompose into independent position and momentum measures. The factor 2/e is the ratio of the two cycle-occupation geometries.

*Relation to §II.17.* Section VIII.11 derives ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2 by the Fourier conjugacy of the position and momentum projections of the McGucken phase. The present route derives a classical bound from an entropy floor. These are two readings of one floor rather than two competing derivations: the entropy floor and the uncertainty floor are the same one-cycle resolution limit of the advance, read as a bound on state count and as a bound on phase-space area respectively. This is why the programme finds that each of the two forces the other — they are one floor expressed in two languages, and their mutual entailment is the signature of a common origin, which the framework names.

### II.28.6 The field-theory extension: an open call, and what §IV.4 supplies Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The advance proceeds from every event of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Manifold, so the object it defines is a field on spacetime rather than a flow on a finite-dimensional phase space, and the extension the programme seeks is the setting in which the Principle is naturally stated.

The programme's open-problems record for Reverse Physics is explicit. It is "actively looking for someone to help generalize Reverse Physics to classical field theory (from finitely many DOFs to continuously many DOFs)"; it asks to "find a suitable Hamiltonian/symplectic formulation of field theory (starting with electromagnetism)"; and it asks to "understand how to generalize count of states/entropy … to field theory." The obstruction is visible in the construction of §II.28.1: extended phase space is (2N + 1)-dimensional for N degrees of freedom, and both the counting form and the divergence-free displacement field are objects on that finite-dimensional manifold. Passing to continuously many degrees of freedom requires a count of states surviving the limit, and the programme records that it does not yet have one.

Section IV.4 of this paper is the field-theoretic setting they describe, reached from the Principle rather than by taking a limit. The x₄-advance field X carries the constraint ∂_μX ∂^μX = −1 enforced by a multiplier ρ, and the three field equations of Proposition IV.3 are the constraint, the continuity equation ∇_μ(ρ u^μ) = 0 with u^μ = −c ∂^μX, and the stress-energy tensor T_μν = ρ u_μu_ν. Their ∇·S = 0 on (q, p, t) and this ∇_μ(ρ u^μ) = 0 on spacetime are the same statement at two levels, and under their own (KE) the phase-space flow projects injectively onto the spacetime congruence, which is why the two agree and where they part company — at caustics. The multiplier is the rest-mass density of the congruence, so what their construction carries as an auxiliary variable is here a physical quantity.

For their third request the framework supplies the count directly. The entropy is the logarithm of the count of x₄-advance states in units of the action per Compton cycle. That count is defined at every event, because the advance proceeds from every event; it is finite per unit area because it is floored at one cycle (§II.28.5); and it is the same count whose horizon reading is the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of §II.10.4(g) and whose event reading is the Born measure of §II.14. A state count native to spacetime, floored, and reproducing both endpoints is the object their third request describes. Its explicit measure-theoretic form is the hybrid measure ℳ = ℝ³ × (ℓ_P · ℤ) of §II.31.4, continuous in the three spatial directions and discrete in the x₄ fibre over each event, with the conjugate momentum in the fibre direction confined to a compact Brillouin zone.

*Scope.* This is offered as a correspondence and a starting point rather than as a completed generalization of their programme. What the framework supplies without qualification is the field-theoretic state count their third request names, together with the field form of the free sector in §II.6.4. A symplectic formulation of field theory in their sense, and electromagnetism treated in that language, are not established here; the gauge sector of this paper is derived through Proposition VI.2 rather than reformulated symplectically, and the input carried by the hybrid measure is stated at §II.31.6. The claim is that the obstruction their record identifies — a count of states surviving the passage to continuously many degrees of freedom — is removed when the count is taken on the expanding wavefront rather than on phase space.
