### II.28.8 The dx₄/dt = ic Completion of the Assumptions of Physics Programme: What Is Established (Physical Object at Each Programme-Identified Location), What Is Explicitly Preserved as the Programme's Own Result (The Equivalences), and the Invitation to Challenge

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The claim of this section is specific and its boundaries are stated directly.

*The claim.* The Assumptions of Physics programme identifies, by its own analysis and with precision, a set of places at which the received formalism rests on a scale, an axiom, or an assumption that the analysis cannot source. Those places are the programme's results rather than its failures: locating them is what the method is for. The McGucken Principle supplies a physical object at each of them, and supplies them from one statement rather than from a list. Where the programme finds that the Born rule and the von Neumann entropy and the third law and the uncertainty bound and the classical limit are one condition seen in different lights, the framework identifies the object whose faces they are — the expanding wavefront of x₄ and its invariant measure — and derives each face from it. That the several conditions converge is itself the evidence: a convergence of that kind is what a single physical source looks like when it is read through a formalism that does not name it.

*What is not claimed.* This paper does not dispute any of the programme's equivalences, and does not claim that its own derivations render them redundant; the equivalences are results about the logical architecture of the received formalism and remain results whatever lies beneath. It is not claimed that dx₄/dt = ic is necessary for a stationary-action principle in the abstract, since the programme exhibits a sufficient alternative set of assumptions on a metric-free manifold. What is claimed is that their manifold carries a time coordinate whose existence the framework sources, and that the specific functional of Proposition IV.1 requires the rate and the signature their construction lacks. The identity of §II.28.2 is a pullback statement on a Lagrangian submanifold and is not an equality of one-forms on the full extended phase space. The field-theory correspondence of §II.28.6 supplies the state count and the field form of the free sector without completing the symplectic formulation. And the programme's Physical Mathematics line — deriving topology and σ-algebras from experimental verifiability, and universal linear, geometric and measure structures from reproducibility and ensembles — addresses the mathematics of experimental science rather than a physical primitive; this framework neither competes with it nor completes it, and the entropic-geometry results of that line are the point at which the two touch.

*Evidence levels.* The action-principle theorem, the classical limit, the unphysicality argument and the Reverse Quantum Mechanics independence result are drawn from published papers and preprints and are engaged on their text. The open-problems record, the statements about the metric in the relativistic material, and the four-step third-law argument are drawn from the programme's lecture and summary material and are engaged as its stated positions rather than as journal results; quotations above are from that material.

*Invitation to challenge.* As with the claims of §§II.11–24, this one is stated with the expectation that it can and should be examined. The claim is falsified in either of two ways. If any terminus listed in §II.28.7 is shown to be sourced within the programme's own resources — the scale h fixed by its thermodynamics rather than introduced, the signature derived rather than supplied, the non-commutativity obtained without an added axiom — then that row is not a completion and should be struck. If a framework other than this one is shown to supply a physical source at every one of those termini from a single statement, the claim of this section would pass to that framework. No such framework has been identified in the survey conducted here.

*The relation, stated once.* Reverse Physics finds that the conditions of the received formalism are one condition in different lights, and stops there by method. The McGucken Principle names what they are conditions of. Each terminus the programme reaches with care is a place where the analysis has run to the edge of the formalism and found that something further is required — a scale, a floor, an axiom, a rate — and each is a place where dx₄/dt = ic says what that something is. The programme's rigor in locating the termini is what makes the completion legible; without its map of where the formalism runs out, a physical source at each point would have nowhere to land.


### II.28.9 The programme classified by channel Under dx₄/dt = ic

The separation of §II.5.8 supplies a compact statement of what the Assumptions of Physics programme carries and what it does not, and the statement explains the pattern of termini catalogued in §II.28.7 rather than merely listing them.

The programme is Channel A throughout. Its objects are an extended phase space, a state count, a two-form, a flow, and a set of assumptions about determinism, reversibility, independence and kinematic equivalence. Every one of these is an algebraic or measure-theoretic condition on a space of states. None of them is a statement that anything propagates: there is no rate in the construction until one is put in by hand at the programme's equation (3), where the flow's temporal component is set to unity, and there is no wavefront anywhere in it. This is not a defect of execution but a consequence of method — Reverse Physics seeks the minimal assumptions sufficient to recover a formalism, and a propagation is not minimal for that purpose, because the formalism can be recovered without one.

The classification predicts where the programme's results stop. A Channel A framework can reach what algebra and invariance can reach: it can prove the action principle equivalent to its three assumptions, it can identify the canonical one-form and observe its resemblance to a four-momentum, it can derive the entropy bounds of its third-law argument up to a scale, and it can prove the independence of the Born rule from the rest of its structure. What it cannot reach is a rate, a signature, a causal cone, or a physical scale, because each of those is a propagation fact rather than a symmetry fact. Every open terminus in the ledger of §II.28.7 is of that kind: the rate set to unity by fiat, the metric and its signature taken as given, the scale h introduced ad hoc, the floor imposed as an axiom, the state count sought for field theory. The programme runs out precisely where Channel B content would be required, and it runs out nowhere else.

What the Principle supplies at each terminus is therefore the missing channel, not a further assumption of the same kind. The rate ic in the slot the programme leaves at unity, the signature by substitution of x₄ = ict, the identification θ|_L = −mc dX of the canonical one-form as the differential of accumulated advance, the scale h as action per Compton cycle, the causal cone that Schuller closure takes as its input, and the state count defined at every event — these are Channel B facts, and they are available because the Principle carries both channels in one statement rather than one channel in an assumption ledger. Section VIII.23 develops the general form of that claim: the presence of two channels in one geometric-dynamical statement is what makes overdetermination possible, and overdetermination is what distinguishes a foundation from a well-executed axiomatization of an existing formalism.

### II.28.10 The gauge hidden in θ, and why every Lagrangian carries it Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The advance has a fixed magnitude and a fixed direction and no fixed origin, and the two consequences of that fact — one about the action, one about the gauge sector — answer a conjecture the programme states and leaves open.

#### The conjecture Under dx₄/dt = ic

The programme's derivation of the action reaches a gauge freedom and stops there. From (DR) the displacement field on extended phase space is divergence-free, hence admits a potential θ with S = −∇×θ; the gauge θ = (p, 0, −H) may be chosen "without loss of generality"; the line integral of θ along a curve is the action. The observation drawn from this is that the gauge freedom in θ is the reason Lagrangians are not unique — "if you study Lagrangian mechanics somebody might have told you that the Lagrangians are not unique for the system. This is why they're not unique. There is a gauge hidden there" (20:06) — and the conjecture drawn from that is stated in the next breath:

> "And I think one should be able to prove that all Lagrangian theory have to be gauge theory in some sense. And this is something that once we are able to expand all of this to field theory is going to be something that we are looking for." (20:06–20:22)

The remainder of the argument establishes that the variation of the action is gauge-invariant: δS is the line integral of θ around the boundary of the surface Σ between a path and its variation, hence by Stokes' theorem the flux of the state-flow through Σ, which vanishes exactly when the path is everywhere tangent to the flow.

Both halves of this have answers under the Principle, and the answers are not of the same kind: the first is an identification already recorded in §II.28.2, the second is a theorem already proved in §II.8.2.

#### The gauge in θ is the zero-point of the advance Under dx₄/dt = ic

Section VIII.22.2 establishes θ|_L = −mc dX on the Lagrangian submanifold of a Hamilton–Jacobi solution, with X the accumulated x₄-advance of Definition IV.4.1. That identity names the gauge freedom directly. A change θ → θ + df alters X by an additive function and leaves dX unchanged; the additive freedom in X is the choice of where the counting of the advance begins. The rate of the advance is what the Principle fixes and is what no gauge transformation touches. So the non-uniqueness of Lagrangians is the non-uniqueness of the x₄-origin, and the gauge-invariant content underneath it is dx₄/dt = ic itself.

The gauge-invariance of the variation follows in the same terms. Their state-flow S is, under the Principle, the advance: the flow of states forward in the parameter is x₄ advancing at ic from every point. Their Stokes argument then reads as a statement about that advance — δS is the flux of x₄-advance through Σ, and it vanishes exactly when the path is everywhere tangent to the advance, so that none of the advance crosses it. Stationary action is the condition that the worldline runs along the advance rather than across it. This is the same conclusion as §II.22.5 reached from the free sector, obtained here from their construction rather than from ℒ_free.

One point in their reading does not carry over, and the disagreement is worth stating because the corrected version is the weaker claim. They conclude from the gauge freedom that the action is "an unphysical quantity." Under the Principle it is not. In the gauge they themselves adopt without loss of generality, θ = −mc dX, so along any solution

∫_γ θ = −mc ΔX = −mc² Δτ,

which is the standard free relativistic action and is the accumulated advance measured in units of mc. What the gauge freedom removes is the origin of the count, not the quantity counted. The action is physical and has no preferred zero — the same status as a potential energy or an x₄-coordinate, and for the same reason, since it is mc times an x₄-coordinate. Their own gauge choice is the one in which this is visible.

#### Why every Lagrangian carries a gauge freedom Under dx₄/dt = ic

The conjecture that all Lagrangian theories must be gauge theories is answered under the Principle at the level of form, and the answer runs through the phase rather than through the origin.

The Principle fixes the magnitude of the advance and its direction and fixes no orthogonal reference within the plane perpendicular to it. The choice of phase reference at each spacetime point is therefore free, and free independently at each point, which is local phase invariance — established at Proposition III.5 and [MG-SM, Theorem 5]. Every Lagrangian sector of ℒ_McG is built from fields coupled to the advance, so every sector inherits that freedom. Demanding that the dynamics be insensitive to a phase reference chosen independently at each point forces a connection, and Proposition VI.2 establishes that the unique Lorentz-invariant, parity-invariant, renormalizable Lagrangian for that connection, first-order in its derivatives, is the Yang-Mills form −¼F^a_μν F^{aμν} for any compact Lie group G ([MG-SM, Theorems 10–11]).

So the two observations are the same gauge structure approached from opposite sides. Their construction finds a gauge freedom in the potential of the state-flow and cannot say what it is a freedom of, because their extended phase space carries no geometry in which a phase could be referenced. The Principle supplies the geometry, and the freedom is the phase reference in the plane perpendicular to the advance. Their conjecture that Lagrangian theory must be gauge theory is, in this framework, the statement that every functional built from an advance with no fixed phase reference carries that indeterminacy, together with the uniqueness result fixing what the resulting gauge Lagrangian must be. The field-theoretic extension they say they are looking for is where the derivation of Proposition VI.2 already operates.

#### Scope Under dx₄/dt = ic

Three limits, stated so that the claim is not read wider than it is.

*What the uniqueness result does and does not fix.* Proposition VI.2 and [MG-SM, Theorems 10–11] force the Yang-Mills form for a given compact G, and they alone do not select G. The selection is supplied separately, in [MG-QFT, §9], by the internal algebra 𝒜_F = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) and the reading of each summand's gauge group as its projective inner-automorphism group; §II.31.6 states what that derivation leaves empirical. The two results are independent and their conjunction is what fixes both the group and the Lagrangian on it.

*The general theorem is not proved.* "Every Lagrangian theory is a gauge theory," quantified over all Lagrangian field theories, is not established here and is not established by them. What is established here is why the Lagrangians forced by the Principle carry a gauge freedom and what that freedom is. A theory not built from the advance is outside the argument's reach.

*Two freedoms, not one.* The free sector carries a reparametrization invariance as well as the phase freedom, and these are distinct. Reparametrization invariance holds because the advance is a geometric fact about a worldline and does not depend on the parameter used to trace it; it is fixed by the einbein elimination of Proposition IV.4. The phase freedom holds because the advance fixes no orthogonal reference; it is fixed by a choice of gauge for the connection. The additive freedom in X identified above is a third and is the global part of the phase freedom, the case f = constant. The Principle sources all three, and they should not be conflated: it is the local phase freedom, not the origin of X, that forces the gauge sector.

### II.28.11 The high-entropy limit, the two arenas as coarse-grainings, and the programme's closing question Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The advance carries one quantum of action per Compton cycle, so a description resolved more coarsely than a cycle cannot register the cycle structure, and what it registers instead is a classical description. The reading given here is developed in [MG-MinkHilb, §§10.12quaterdecies–quindecies] and [MG-Thermo, Theorem 22.5]; the present section states the part that bears on the Lagrangian program and adds three items from the published paper that those treatments do not use.

#### The result and what it establishes Under dx₄/dt = ic

[Carcassi-Landini-Aidala 2026] establishes that classical mechanics is the high-entropy limit of quantum mechanics: high entropy masks quantum effects, and mixed states of sufficiently high entropy are approximated by classical distributions over phase space. The identity carrying the result is that entropy is the logarithm of the count of states measured in units of ℏ, so that the mathematical limit ℏ → 0 is the same operation as setting the entropy of pure states to −∞, and the physically meaningful form of the limit is S ≫ 0 rather than a limit taken on a constant. The mechanism is a stretching map on phase space, realized quantum-mechanically as a purely dissipative Lindblad evolution with jump operator a†, which rescales anti-normally ordered expectations by λ^(n+m) and takes [X̂, P̂] = iℏ/λ, so that λ → ∞ performs the group contraction from the Moyal bracket to the Poisson bracket.

The result is stated as independent of mechanism by design: "this limit is therefore independent of what interpretation one may give to either quantum mechanics or entropy, and from the reason, the mechanism, that makes a high-entropy description suitable," with the parallel drawn to the low-speed limit, where "no one tries to find a reason, a mechanism, as to why speeds become low in certain regimes." That is a methodological choice of the kind §II.30.1 records, and it is what leaves the floor being masked against unaccounted for.

#### The limit as loss of x₄-resolution, and the two arenas as its two coarse-grainings

Under the Principle the limit has a definite geometric structure. Since ℏ is the action per Compton cycle of the advance, ℏ → 0 is the regime in which the cycle falls below every resolved scale, so the discrete advance is coarse-grained into a continuum and the wavefront is indistinguishable from a classical one. Their S ≫ 0 is loss of x₄-resolution.

[MG-MinkHilb, §10.12quaterdecies] carries this further, and the further step is what connects their result to the two arenas the corpus derives. Minkowski space is the coordinate integral ∫ic dt = ict, which sums over the individual cycles and delivers a continuous coordinate in which the cycle structure is no longer resolved. The Born density is the modulus-frozen reading, in which the squaring discards the phase. Each is obtained from the McGucken Sphere by summing over a distinguishable structure — the cycle count in the first case, the phase in the second — and summing over a distinguishable structure is, in their own state-counting, an increase of entropy by the logarithm of the number of collapsed alternatives. Their own two-slit illustration is the second case exactly: the maximally mixed state makes a randomized phase indistinguishable from a randomized path, so the phase degree of freedom has been summed over. The two arenas are therefore higher-entropy readings of one lower-entropy object, and the object is the expanding Sphere with its cycles and phase intact.

The scope of that identification is stated at [MG-MinkHilb, §10.12quaterdecies]: their entropy is the von Neumann entropy of mixed states, the concealment at issue is an information coarse-graining, and the two agree for these two structures because the cycle count and the phase are distinguishable degrees of freedom whose loss is an increase in state count. It is not claimed that every coarse-graining in the framework is thermodynamic entropy.

#### The floor as the condition that makes the arenas integrable Under dx₄/dt = ic

The one-cycle floor of §II.28.5 has a second role that bears directly on the construction of ℒ_McG. Both arenas are integrals of the advance, and an integral is a sum over increments. Were the increments unbounded below, the sum would run over a continuum of infinitesimal expansions with no smallest cell, no well-defined measure would exist, and the construction would carry the pathology that the entropy logarithm carries without its cell h — the same gap one level down. The floor closes both at once: the advance is quantized at one cycle, the sum has a smallest cell, and each integral converges to a space carrying a proper measure — Lebesgue on the spatial slice, and the SO(3)-invariant measure on rays that the Born reading requires ([MG-MinkHilb, §10.12quindecies]).

The order is logical rather than causal. All three — the entropy floor, the metric, and the Hilbert space — descend from dx₄/dt = ic, and the floor is the measure-theoretic precondition of the integration rather than a separate cause upstream of the other two. In field theory the same requirement returns as the hybrid measure of §II.31.4, where the discreteness in the x₄ fibre is what bounds the loop integrals; the floor that makes the entropy well-defined and the floor that makes the field-theoretic measure well-defined are the same floor.

#### Three items from the published paper Under dx₄/dt = ic

*Atomic stability read off the entropy floor.* The paper draws a consequence its earlier presentations do not: "classical states for which σ_x σ_p < ℏ/e are states with negative entropy, which imply a breakdown of thermodynamics. It is no wonder, then, electrons cannot fall on the nucleus or that classical mechanics gives us the wrong spectra for black-body radiation. Classical mechanics fails at low entropy." Under the Principle the floor whose violation this identifies is the one-cycle floor, so the stability of the atom against radiative collapse and the failure of the Rayleigh–Jeans law are two instances of the same fact: a description cannot resolve below one Compton cycle of the advance. The framework does not add a mechanism to their argument here; it names what the floor is, and the naming makes the two failures instances of one geometric limit rather than two thermodynamic coincidences.

*Spin as exempt from the limit.* "The maximum entropy attainable by a quantum system is the logarithm of the dimension of the corresponding Hilbert space, [so] the high-entropy limit exists only for infinite-dimensional spaces. This explains why spin, which lives in a finite-dimensional space, is an intrinsically quantum property." The framework reaches the same exemption from the other side. Spin is the 4π-periodicity of the McGucken-Sphere SO(3) lift on Cl(1,3)⁺ Weyl spinors (§II.31.2), which is a property of the geometry of the advance rather than a property of a resolution scale, so no amount of coarse-graining reaches it. Their dimensional argument and this geometric one identify the same exemption, and the geometric one says what the exempt structure is.

*The two axes of their four-quadrant figure.* The paper opens with the four-quadrant diagram whose axes are Speed and Entropy, replacing the usual size axis, and closes with the statement that ℏ → 0 should be read as S ≫ 0 in the same way that c → ∞ should be read as v ≪ c. Under the Principle the two axes are the two parameters of one advance: c is its rate and ℏ the action per cycle of it. A worldline at v ≪ c spends almost none of its four-speed budget on spatial motion (Proposition III.2); a description at S ≫ 0 is coarse compared with one cycle of the same motion. Their two limits stand in a formal parallel that their method takes as an analogy; here the parallel is expected, because the two constants bounding the diagram are two attributes of a single geometric fact (§II.16). Their own reading of quantization as the imposition of an entropy floor completes the picture: the ℏ-floor and the c-ceiling are the two edges of one parameter space.

#### The closing question Under dx₄/dt = ic

The paper ends with a question rather than a claim: "we wonder whether it can be proven that quantum mechanics is the only way to fix the low-entropy range of classical mechanics. That is, is quantum mechanics the only theory that can recover classical mechanics at high entropy? To us, this is a question whose answer would be interesting regardless of the outcome."

Their own §II.4 narrows what an answer would have to establish: "if by classical limit we mean the group contraction, then the only way to achieve it is through the rescaling of the commutator between X and P," and the Moyal bracket is the unique one-parameter Lie-algebraic deformation of the Poisson bracket. The question therefore reduces to what fixes the commutator, and the corpus answers it on two sides.

On the deformation side the answer is theirs: Moyal uniqueness says there is one way to impose the floor once the floor is to be imposed by a deformation of the bracket. On the physical side the answer is the two-route derivation of §II.12.7 together with the closure of §II.12.3: [q̂, p̂] = iℏ follows from dx₄/dt = ic along two chains that share no intermediate machinery, and the Stone–von Neumann theorem then fixes the representation up to unitary equivalence, excluding non-quantum alternatives at that step. The bracket their contraction rescales is not a free choice among candidates; it is the projection of the x₄-advance onto the conjugate plane, with its i the perpendicularity of x₄ and its ℏ the action per cycle.

*Scope of that answer.* Stone–von Neumann fixes the representation given the canonical relation, and the two-route result fixes which relation the advance produces. Together they establish that among theories imposing the low-entropy floor by non-commutativity, the bracket and its representation are determined. A theory flooring the entropy by some other means is outside what the argument excludes. Their question as put is broader than the answer available here, and the corresponding claim of [MG-MinkHilb, §10.12quindecies] — that the deformation-side and primitive-side answers agree "within their respective classes" — is the same qualification stated from the other direction.

## II.29. Overdetermination as the Criterion for a Foundation, and the Dual-Channel Reading at Four Levels: Formulation, Ontology, Dynamics, and Causality Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The McGucken Principle states that the fourth dimension is expanding at the rate c from every point of spacetime, dx₄/dt = ic. Section III.8 separated the two contents carried by that statement — Channel A, the algebraic-symmetry structure, and Channel B, the geometric-propagation — and §II.12.7 exhibited the two disjoint derivational chains those channels support, Propositions H.1–H.5 and Propositions L.1–L.6, each terminating in the canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ. The present section draws the two consequences of that architecture that bear on the standing of ℒ_McG as a whole.

The first consequence is evidentiary. When one claim follows from one principle along two chains that share no intermediate machinery, the claim is *overdetermined* relative to the principle. Section VIII.23.1 develops overdetermination as a general pattern, distinguishes it from equivalence in the sense of Feynman and Stone–von Neumann, exhibits four historical instances of the pattern, and states the three-part criterion it yields for distinguishing a foundation from a reformulation. The criterion is then applied to ℒ_McG.

The second consequence is that the dual-channel reading is not confined to the question of which formulation of quantum mechanics is primary. The same separation applies, unchanged, at three further levels of description: the ontological level, where it produces wave/particle duality (§II.29.2); the dynamical level, where it produces the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures together with a geometric proof of their equivalence (§II.29.3); and the causal/correlational level, where it produces the coexistence of the local operator algebra of quantum field theory with the nonlocal Bell correlations of entangled systems (§II.29.4). Section VIII.23.5 assembles the four levels and states what their agreement establishes. The material of this section is developed at length in the companion papers [MG-TwoRoutes], [MG-Nonlocality] and [MG-Equiv]; the present section states it in the form the Lagrangian program uses, with proofs supplied where the argument turns on them.

### II.29.1 The Overdetermination Principle Under dx₄/dt = ic

#### II.29.1.1 The pattern Under dx₄/dt = ic

A claim is *overdetermined* relative to a principle when it follows from the principle along two or more derivational chains that share no essential intermediate machinery. The pattern has exactly three components.

*A common start.* One principle serves as the point of departure for every chain. In the case at hand the common start is dx₄/dt = ic.

*A common end.* One claim serves as the destination of every chain. In the case at hand the common end is [q̂, p̂] = iℏ.

*Disjoint intermediates.* The chains must not share essential machinery. If one chain's intermediate content is contained in the other's, or if both pass through the same theorem at a corresponding step, the two are variants of a single derivation rather than independent derivations. The disjointness required is physical, not cosmetic: different mathematical machinery, different content drawn from the starting principle, different intermediate theorems, with agreement only at the two endpoints.

All three components are present in §II.12.7. The start is dx₄/dt = ic; the end is [q̂, p̂] = iℏ; and the intermediate catalog compiled at the close of that section shows the two chains sharing no theorem, no channel of the Principle's content, and no mathematical apparatus. The Hamiltonian chain consumes Channel A and passes through the Minkowski metric, Stone's theorem, the configuration representation, the direct commutator computation, and the Stone–von Neumann uniqueness theorem. The Lagrangian chain consumes Channel B and passes through Huygens' principle, iterated spherical expansion, Compton-frequency phase accumulation, the Feynman kernel, and Gaussian integration. Neither chain invokes a step of the other.

#### II.29.1.2 Why the pattern carries weight Under dx₄/dt = ic

Three reasons, of increasing depth.

*Confirmation.* A claim established by two independent methods is confirmed twice independently. In mathematics the availability of several proofs of a theorem is not redundancy; it is evidence that the theorem is a consequence of the axioms rather than an artifact of a proof technique. The analogue in physics is exact. The commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ is not an artifact of having elected to work through Stone's theorem, nor an artifact of having elected to work through Huygens' principle. It follows through both.

*Illumination.* Different proofs of one theorem expose different aspects of it. The Hamiltonian route exhibits the commutation relation as an algebraic-symmetry consequence of translation invariance on a complex Hilbert space. The Lagrangian route exhibits the same relation as a geometric-propagation consequence of spherical expansion in spacetime. Both characterizations are correct, and each is concealed by the other in the standard presentations. Taken together the two routes show that the commutation relation is simultaneously an algebraic fact and a geometric fact. A framework reaching the relation by one route exhibits one of its two aspects.

*Discrimination between a foundation and a reformulation.* This is the reason that matters for the present paper. A reformulation of existing physics in new variables can reach known results along its own chain, but it is constrained to reach them by construction: it was engineered to reproduce them. A correct foundation generates known results as consequences, and if it carries enough content it generates the same consequence along several independent chains. When that occurs, the overdetermination is evidence that the framework was not engineered to produce the result, because engineering a result along one chain does not engineer it along a disjoint second chain. This was Einstein's own argument for special relativity: the Lorentz transformations derived from the relativity principle together with the invariance of c are the same transformations derived from the form invariance of Maxwell's equations, and the agreement of two independent starting points was his evidence that relativity is a kinematic principle applying to all physics rather than a device for saving electrodynamic phenomena.

#### II.29.1.3 Overdetermination is not equivalence Under dx₄/dt = ic

A confusion worth forestalling is between overdetermination in the present sense and equivalence in the sense of Feynman 1948 and Stone–von Neumann 1931–1932.

Equivalence of the Hamiltonian and Lagrangian formulations of quantum mechanics is the claim that both yield the same predictions for every measurable quantity, established by Feynman's derivation of the Schrödinger equation from the path integral and by the Stone–von Neumann uniqueness of the Schrödinger representation. Equivalence is bidirectional: each formulation is derivable from the other.

Overdetermination is a claim from above: one principle yields both formulations along chains that do not pass through each other. The Hamiltonian route of §II.12.7 does not use the path integral; the Lagrangian route does not use Stone's theorem or the direct commutator.

Equivalence is compatible with overdetermination and distinct from it. Equivalence says the two formulations describe the same physics; overdetermination says they descend independently from a common source. Equivalence is a property of quantum mechanics as it stands; overdetermination is a property of a framework that derives quantum mechanics. The distinction matters because equivalence alone identifies no foundation: Feynman's demonstration that the path integral and the operator formalism agree does not settle whether both descend from a common principle. It settles only that, given both as starting points, they describe the same physics. The question "which is primary?" is left open by equivalence theorems, and the answer supplied here is that neither is — both descend from dx₄/dt = ic as the two readings of its dual-channel content.

#### II.29.1.4 The pattern in the historical record Under dx₄/dt = ic

The two-route derivation is not the first overdetermination in physics. Four instances fix the pattern.

*Special relativity.* The Lorentz transformations follow from the Einstein postulates through the kinematic analysis of §§II.4–5 of Einstein 1905, and independently from the form invariance of Maxwell's equations under the transformations Lorentz had already identified on electrodynamic grounds. The agreement of the kinematic route with the electromagnetic route was Einstein's evidence that relativity applies to all physics rather than to electromagnetism alone.

*Noether's first theorem.* Conservation of energy follows in Hamiltonian mechanics as the Noether charge of time-translation symmetry of the Hamiltonian, and independently in Lagrangian mechanics as the Noether charge of time-translation symmetry of the Lagrangian. The overdetermination of the conservation law by the two formulations is the content of Noether's theorem as a bridge between them.

*Hawking radiation.* Hawking's 1975 derivation proceeds through a Bogoliubov-coefficient analysis of quantum field theory on a black-hole background. The independent Euclidean derivation proceeds through the observation that the Wick rotation of the black-hole metric is a smooth cap whose periodicity in imaginary time equals the inverse Hawking temperature. The two reach T_H = ℏκ/(2πck_B) through disjoint machinery, and the agreement is taken as evidence that the effect is a genuine consequence of quantum field theory on a curved background rather than an artifact of a calculational route.

*The Gauss–Bonnet theorem.* At the mathematical level, the integral of the Gaussian curvature over a closed surface equals 2π times the Euler characteristic. The result follows from local differential geometry by curvature integration and independently from algebraic topology by identification of the Euler characteristic as a topological invariant. The agreement is evidence that the theorem is a genuine bridge between curvature and topology rather than a coincidence of two computations.

In each instance the pattern — two independent chains, one start, one end — is what distinguishes a genuine consequence from an artifact of calculational choice. The two-route derivation of the canonical commutation relation from dx₄/dt = ic is the first appearance of the pattern in the foundations of quantum mechanics: the first occasion on which the canonical commutation relation has been reached from a single physical principle along two chains of disjoint machinery.

#### II.29.1.5 The criterion, and its application to ℒ_McG Under dx₄/dt = ic

The discussion yields a criterion for distinguishing a foundation from a reformulation or an equivalence theorem. A framework qualifies as a foundation for a body of physics if and only if:

(i) it starts from a principle that is not itself a reformulation of the physics to be derived;

(ii) it derives the known results of that physics as consequences of the principle rather than importing them as inputs; and

(iii) it exhibits overdetermination — at least one important result of that physics is reached along several disjoint chains from the principle.

ℒ_McG satisfies all three. On (i), dx₄/dt = ic is a geometric-dynamical statement about a physical fourth axis in spacetime, not a rewriting of the Lagrangian it forces. On (ii), the four sectors of Theorem VI.1 together with the Higgs sector of Theorem VI.2 are derived as consequences, with the empirical inputs of the Standard Model reduced accordingly (§II.27.1). On (iii), overdetermination is exhibited at four places in the present paper and its companions.

*The canonical commutation relation*, through Propositions H.1–H.5 and Propositions L.1–L.6 (§II.12.7).

*Huygens' principle*, through the direct spherical-expansion route of [MG-HLA] and through the retarded Green's-function route of [MG-Proof], which pass through no common theorem.

*The Second Law of Thermodynamics*, through the Brownian-motion route of [MG-Entropy], through the x₄-directionality route of [MG-Singular], and through the conservation-law and arrow-of-time route of §II.20. Three chains, not two.

*The Einstein–Hilbert sector*, through the Schuller closure route of Proposition VI.3 and through the Jacobson horizon-thermodynamic route of Remark VI.3.1. The former consumes the universal principal polynomial as its input; the latter consumes the horizon mode count on null hypersurfaces. Both terminate in the same action with the same coefficient c⁴/16πG.

Remark VIII.23.1 (what fails the criterion). The frameworks surveyed in [MG-TwoRoutes, §VI] fail at (i) or (iii) or both. Feynman's 1948 path integral fails (i): it is a reformulation of existing quantum mechanics, and it has no principle with respect to which overdetermination could be exhibited. Nelson's stochastic mechanics passes (i) by starting from a stochastic postulate and fails (iii): it reaches the Schrödinger equation along one route and derives neither the commutation relation nor the representation structure separately. Geometric quantization fails (i), since classical phase space is itself a rewriting of classical mechanics, and fails (iii), reaching the operator formulation along a single route. The pattern across the survey is uniform. The channel taxonomy of §II.5.8.3 explains why: overdetermination of the kind at issue requires two channels of content in the starting principle, and a framework carrying one channel has only one chain available to it.

### II.29.2 The Ontological Level: Wave and Particle Under dx₄/dt = ic

#### II.29.2.1 The reading Under dx₄/dt = ic

Under dx₄/dt = ic, wave/particle duality is not a puzzle requiring an interpretive scheme. It is the dual-channel content read at the ontological level — at the level of what quantum objects are.

*Channel B generates the wave aspect.* The spherical symmetry of x₄'s expansion about every spacetime point is Huygens' principle (Proposition L.1), and iterated Huygens composition (Proposition L.2) generates wavefront propagation. The interference observed in double-slit geometries is the superposition of Huygens wavelets from the two apertures; the diffraction observed in single-slit geometries is the superposition of wavelets from each point of one aperture. The matter wavelength λ_dB = h/p observed by Davisson and Germer, by Thomson, and in every subsequent matter-wave experiment is the x₄-phase accumulation of matter per unit of spatial displacement, at the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ of Proposition L.3.

*Channel A generates the particle aspect.* The invariance of x₄'s advance under spacetime translations gives, by Stone's theorem (Proposition H.2), self-adjoint generators whose eigenvalues are the four-momenta of the theory (Proposition H.3). A detection event at a definite pixel is an eigenvalue event of the position observable. The quantized exchanges of energy and momentum observed in the photoelectric effect and in Compton scattering are eigenvalue exchanges of the Channel A observables, conserved event by event. The Heisenberg relation Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2, which is the quantitative form of the complementarity between the two aspects, is by [MG-Uncertainty] a theorem about the Fourier duality of the x₄-phase, whose algebraic content is Channel A and whose propagation is Channel B.

A quantum object traversing a two-slit apparatus does both at once. Its Channel B content is the wavefront reaching both apertures and interfering at the screen. Its Channel A content is the eigenvalue event at one pixel. There is no contradiction, because the two are not competing descriptions of one thing; they are two simultaneous readings of one geometric fact, corresponding to two distinct contents present in the statement of the Principle.

#### II.29.2.2 The classical puzzles Under dx₄/dt = ic

*The two-slit puzzle.* Interference requires both apertures because the wavelets from both are needed for the superposition; closing one removes one family of wavelets. The pattern is lost when which-path information is obtained because a which-path measurement is an eigenvalue event of the aperture-position observable, and registering an eigenvalue is a Channel A act on a system whose interference is a Channel B phenomenon. The suppression is the consequence of having elected to read one channel at the measurement, not a philosophical difficulty requiring complementarity as a doctrine.

*The delayed-choice puzzle.* The decision to register wave or particle behavior may be taken after the object has traversed the apparatus because both readings are available at every point of the path, not manufactured retroactively by the measurement. The Channel B wavefront is present throughout the apparatus; the Channel A eigenvalue event occurs at the detector. The delayed choice is a choice of which channel to register at the detector, not an alteration of what occurred earlier.

*The quantum-eraser puzzle.* Interference is recoverable after which-path information has been obtained and erased because the two channels are not ordered in time — the eigenvalue structure and the wavefront structure coexist at every spacetime point. Obtaining and erasing which-path information are operational choices about which channel to correlate with the final detection; neither alters the dual-channel content of the Principle. The eraser experiments demonstrate the simultaneity of the two channels rather than retroactive causation.

*The matter-wave and molecular-interference puzzles.* Electrons, neutrons, atoms and molecules interfere because Channel B applies to anything coupled to x₄'s oscillation, with wavelength λ = h/(Mv) scaled by the total mass. For sufficiently low velocities the wavelength stays comparable to the grating period even for very large molecules, which is why interference has been observed for C₆₀ and C₇₀ fullerenes, for phthalocyanine, and for molecules of some thousands of atomic mass units. There is no lower bound on wave behavior imposed by a boundary between a quantum and a classical realm, because on the present account there is no such boundary: all matter carries Channel B content by virtue of its coupling to the advance of x₄.

Remark VIII.23.2 (dissolution rather than interpretation). Complementarity, pilot waves, branching, decoherence, relational states and epistemic reinterpretation each accept the dual aspect as irreducible and supply a scheme for living with it. Under the present reading the duality is derived, and derived twice over from one statement. The distinction between interpreting a duality and deriving it is the same distinction drawn in §II.29.1.3 between equivalence and overdetermination, applied at the ontological level.

### II.29.3 The Dynamical Level: The Schrödinger and Heisenberg Pictures, Read Through dx₄/dt = ic

#### II.29.3.1 The reading Under dx₄/dt = ic

Quantum-mechanical time evolution admits two representations. In the Schrödinger picture, states evolve under iℏ d|ψ(t)⟩/dt = Ĥ|ψ(t)⟩ while operators are held fixed. In the Heisenberg picture, operators evolve under iℏ dÂ(t)/dt = [Â(t), Ĥ] while states are held fixed. The two are related by the unitary Û(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) and agree on every expectation value.

Under dx₄/dt = ic the two pictures are the dual-channel reading at the dynamical level. Channel B, the propagation, updates the state: the wavefront is carried forward by the advance of x₄, in the path-integral sense of Propositions L.1–L.5. Channel A, the algebra, updates the observable: the algebraic definition of the observable is carried into the time-translated frame, in the matrix-mechanical sense of Heisenberg's original treatment of observables as the primary dynamical objects. One physical process — the advance of x₄ by ic·t from every spacetime point — is represented in two ways, according to which mathematical object is updated to record it.

This reading supplies more than a labelling. It supplies a geometric proof of the equivalence of the two pictures, in which the equality of expectation values follows from the physics of x₄'s advance rather than from a manipulation of the evolution operator.

#### II.29.3.2 The equivalence theorem Under dx₄/dt = ic

**Theorem VIII.23.1 (Schrödinger–Heisenberg equivalence from dx₄/dt = ic).** Let ℋ be the complex Hilbert space of states of a physical system, let Ĥ be the self-adjoint generator of time translations on ℋ, let Û(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) be the associated one-parameter unitary group, let |ψ⟩ ∈ ℋ, and let Â = Â† be an observable on ℋ. Define the Schrödinger-picture state |ψ_S(t)⟩ = Û(t)|ψ⟩ with Â held fixed, and the Heisenberg-picture observable Â_H(t) = Û(t)†ÂÛ(t) with |ψ⟩ held fixed. Then

⟨ψ_S(t)| Â |ψ_S(t)⟩ = ⟨ψ| Â_H(t) |ψ⟩,

and under the McGucken Principle this equality holds not as an algebraic identity of unitary conjugation but as a consequence of the geometry of dx₄/dt = ic: both sides compute the expectation of the same observable after the same physical process — the advance of x₄ by ic·t from every spacetime point — with the two sides differing only in which object is updated to record the advance.

The proof proceeds through three lemmas: the physical identification of Û(t) (Lemma VIII.23.A), the two actions of Û(t) corresponding to the two channels (Lemma VIII.23.B), and the preservation of expectation values under either action (Lemma VIII.23.C).

**Lemma VIII.23.A (the evolution operator as the Hilbert-space implementation of x₄'s advance).** The one-parameter unitary group Û(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) is the operator implementation on ℋ of x₄'s advance by ic·t. Specifically: (i) the generator Ĥ is the Noether charge of the temporal uniformity of that advance; (ii) the factor i in the exponent is the perpendicularity marker of x₄, the same i as in x₄ = ict; (iii) the factor ℏ is the action per complete x₄-oscillation cycle at the Planck frequency, as identified in [MG-Constants, §V].

*Proof.* The one-parameter unitary group representing time translations on ℋ is strongly continuous, since physical predictions depend continuously on the elapsed parameter. Stone's theorem therefore gives Û(t) = exp(−itĤ/ℏ) for a densely defined self-adjoint Ĥ, the factor i being forced by the joint requirements of unitarity, Û(t)Û(t)† = 𝟙, and self-adjointness of the generator, Ĥ = Ĥ†. This is the same appeal to Stone's theorem made in Proposition H.2 for the spatial translation subgroup, applied here to the time-translation subgroup; the derivational chain is identical and the group is different. That the i so produced is the i of x₄ = ict is the content of Proposition H.2 together with Proposition III.1: the group whose generators Stone's theorem produces is the isometry group of the Minkowski metric, and the Minkowski metric is the substitution of x₄ = ict into a Euclidean form. Dimensional consistency is immediate — Ĥ carries dimensions of energy and ℏ of action, so Ĥt/ℏ is dimensionless, the factor c being carried inside Ĥ. The identification of ℏ as the action accumulated per complete cycle of the x₄-oscillation at the Planck frequency f_P = 1/t_P is established in [MG-Constants, §V] and is the same identification used in Proposition L.3. That Ĥ is the Noether charge of time-translation symmetry follows from the temporal uniformity of the advance — dx₄/dt = ic holds at every spacetime point, so translation in the parameter is a symmetry of the Principle — by the Noether construction of Remark III.4.1. Every ingredient of Û(t) is therefore fixed by dx₄/dt = ic. ∎

**Lemma VIII.23.B (the two actions of Û(t)).** The unitary Û(t) of Lemma VIII.23.A admits two actions carrying a description of the system at parameter 0 to a description at parameter t:

(B1) *the Channel B action*, in which Û(t) acts on the state, |ψ⟩ ↦ |ψ_S(t)⟩ = Û(t)|ψ⟩, with observables fixed. Geometrically this implements the advance of x₄ as the forward propagation of the state's wavefront, in the sense of Propositions L.1–L.5;

(B2) *the Channel A action*, in which Û(t) acts on the observable by conjugation, Â ↦ Â_H(t) = Û(t)†ÂÛ(t), with the state fixed. Geometrically this implements the advance of x₄ as the carrying of the observable's algebraic definition into the translated frame.

*Proof.* Both actions follow from unitarity. For any operator Ô and any states |ψ⟩, |φ⟩, inserting 𝟙 = Û(t)Û(t)† preserves the matrix element, and the insertions may be distributed across the factors:

⟨φ|Ô|ψ⟩ = ⟨φ|[Û(t)Û(t)†] Ô [Û(t)Û(t)†]|ψ⟩ = ⟨φ_S(t)| Ô_H(t) |ψ_S(t)⟩,

with |ψ_S(t)⟩ = Û(t)|ψ⟩, |φ_S(t)⟩ = Û(t)|φ⟩ and Ô_H(t) = Û(t)†ÔÛ(t). Concentrating both insertions on the state vectors gives the pure Channel B reading; concentrating both on the operator gives the pure Channel A reading; distributing them between the two gives the intermediate pictures, of which the interaction picture is the case in which the free and interacting parts of Ĥ are assigned to the two objects separately. the physics of the lemma is that the advance of x₄ by ic·t is one process, and that the choice of which object records it is a choice of representation. The two pure readings are the extreme cases of the dual-channel content, and they are equivalent because both record the same advance on the same system. ∎

**Lemma VIII.23.C (preservation of expectation values).** For every |ψ⟩ ∈ ℋ and every observable Â = Â†,

⟨Â⟩(t) := ⟨ψ_S(t)| Â |ψ_S(t)⟩ = ⟨ψ| Â_H(t) |ψ⟩,

independently of which reading is chosen.

*Proof.* Using Û(t)Û(t)† = Û(t)†Û(t) = 𝟙 with the definitions of Lemma VIII.23.B,

⟨ψ_S(t)| Â |ψ_S(t)⟩ = [Û(t)|ψ⟩]† Â [Û(t)|ψ⟩] = ⟨ψ| Û(t)† Â Û(t) |ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ| Â_H(t) |ψ⟩. ∎

*Proof of Theorem VIII.23.1.* Apply Lemma VIII.23.C to the state |ψ⟩ and observable Â of the statement. ∎

**Corollary VIII.23.D (picture independence of every prediction).** Every quantum-mechanical prediction expressible through expectation values — transition probabilities, scattering amplitudes, correlation functions, time-ordered products, S-matrix entries — takes the same value in the Schrödinger picture, in the Heisenberg picture, and in every intermediate picture.

*Proof.* Every such prediction is a sum, product or integral of matrix elements ⟨φ| Ô₁(t₁) ⋯ Ô_n(t_n) |ψ⟩, reducible to expectation-value form by the polarization identities. Each matrix element is picture-independent by Lemmas VIII.23.B and VIII.23.C, the insertions Û(t_k)Û(t_k)† being distributable across states and operators in any consistent way, and the composite is therefore picture-independent as well. ∎

#### II.29.3.3 In what sense the proof is geometric Under dx₄/dt = ic

The algebra of Lemma VIII.23.C is the algebra of the textbook proof of the equivalence, found in Schrödinger's third 1926 paper, in von Neumann 1932, in Dirac 1930, and in every modern treatment. The step ⟨Û(t)ψ|Â|Û(t)ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ|Û(t)†ÂÛ(t)|ψ⟩ is the same manipulation in all of them. What distinguishes the present proof is not the algebra but the physical identification of the objects the algebra manipulates, which is supplied by Lemmas VIII.23.A and VIII.23.B.

The textbook proof establishes that the two pictures agree and leaves three questions standing: why the evolution operator has the exponential form it has, why the exponent carries a factor i, and why it carries a factor ℏ. Each is answered here rather than assumed. The exponential form follows from Stone's theorem applied to a strongly continuous unitary representation of the time-translation group, which is a symmetry of the Principle because the advance is uniform. The i is the perpendicularity of x₄ to the three spatial dimensions, entering the exponent by the same route it enters the metric. The ℏ is the action accumulated per complete x₄-cycle. The equality of the two sides is then not an accident of unitary algebra but the statement that two records of one physical advance agree.

Remark VIII.23.3 (the equivalence and the equivalence theorems). The relation of Theorem VIII.23.1 to the classical equivalence results is exactly the relation set out in §II.29.1.3. Schrödinger and von Neumann establish that the two pictures agree. Theorem VIII.23.1 establishes why they agree: because both record one advance of x₄, and the two channels of the Principle's content are the two ways of recording it. The classical result is a theorem within quantum mechanics; the present one is a theorem about the descent of quantum mechanics from a geometric principle.

### II.29.4 The Causal and Correlational Level: Locality and Nonlocality Under dx₄/dt = ic

#### II.29.4.1 The tension Under dx₄/dt = ic

Quantum mechanics carries two features that have coexisted in apparent tension since 1935. On one side it possesses a local operator algebra: observables are defined pointwise, operators at spacelike separation commute, [Ô(x), Ô(y)] = 0 for (x − y)² > 0, and the theory satisfies microcausality in the sense formalized by Wightman, by Haag and Kastler, and by the subsequent algebraic tradition. On the other side it exhibits correlations between spatially separated entangled systems that no local hidden-variable theory reproduces: the singlet correlation E(a,b) = −cos θ_ab violates the Bell inequalities, and the violation is confirmed by the Aspect experiments of the early 1980s and by the loophole-closing experiments of 2015 at Delft, at NIST and in Vienna.

The two features have been developed within separate accounts — microcausality as an axiom of quantum field theory, nonlocal correlation as a result within entanglement theory — and no prior foundation has supplied both as theorems of one principle along disjoint channels of that principle's content.

#### II.29.4.2 The reading Under dx₄/dt = ic

*Channel A forces locality and microcausality.* The algebraic-symmetry structure — uniformity of the rate, invariance under the isometries, Lorentz covariance of the advance — is what forces the Minkowski metric by Proposition III.1. The Minkowski metric carries the light-cone causal structure, spacelike-separated events are causally disconnected in it, and quantum operators respecting that structure commute at spacelike separation. Microcausality is therefore a Channel A theorem, reached along the same chain that produced the canonical commutation relation in §II.12.7: dx₄/dt = ic → Minkowski metric → invariant causal structure → [Ô(x), Ô(y)] = 0 for (x − y)² > 0.

*Channel B forces the nonlocal correlations.* The geometric-propagation — spherical expansion at rate c from every spacetime point — is what forces Huygens' principle, the McGucken Sphere and the wavefront structure of propagation, by Proposition L.1. The same Sphere that carries the wave aspect of §II.29.2 and the path measure of the Lagrangian route carries the correlations of entanglement. Two particles created at a common spacetime event share one McGucken Sphere. Because a photon has v_x4 = 0 — it does not advance in x₄ along a null worldline (§II.5.6) — the members of an entangled photon pair remain at one x₄-coordinate for all subsequent parameter values regardless of their spatial separation, and the four-dimensional interval between them remains null throughout. Along the null worldline there is neither proper time nor proper distance between the two events. The singlet correlation E(a,b) = −cos θ_ab then follows from the SO(3) Haar-measure symmetry of the shared Sphere, with no local hidden variable required [MG-Twistor, Proposition X.6]. This is the identification recorded in [MG-Equiv]: what presents as nonlocality in three dimensions is the three-dimensional shadow of four-dimensional x₄-coincidence on the light cone.

The two features are therefore two readings of one principle through the same two channels that produced the Hamiltonian and Lagrangian formulations. Their coexistence, understood since Bell 1964 as a genuine feature of the theory requiring reconciliation, is the fourth appearance of the dual-channel separation.

#### II.29.4.3 The six senses in which the McGucken Sphere is one object Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Channel B reading rests on a specific geometric claim: that the expanding Sphere is a single object whose spatially separated points share a common identity traceable to one local origin. The claim is established in [MG-Nonlocality, §4] through six frameworks, each identifying the wavefront as a locality in a distinct sense. They are recorded here because each is a statement about the same geometry that §II.6.4.4 uses for the caustic bound and that Proposition VI.3 uses for the causal cone.

(i) *Foliation.* The family of Spheres parameterized by t foliates three-space, each Sphere Σ(t) being a leaf. Points on one leaf share a common membership in one submanifold, separated by the transverse structure from points on other leaves.

(ii) *Level sets of a distance function.* The wavefront is the level set d(x) = ct of the distance from the origin of the expansion. Every point on it is equidistant from that origin in the induced metric.

(iii) *Huygens caustic.* The wavefront is the envelope of the secondary wavelets emitted from every point of the preceding wavefront, and therefore the boundary between the region that has received the disturbance and the region that has not. Every point on it shares the same causal status as a boundary point of the causal future of the origin event.

(iv) *Contact geometry.* In the jet space with coordinates (x, y, z, t) the expanding wavefront traces a cone that is a Legendrian submanifold of the contact structure. Membership is fixed by the contact distribution rather than by position alone.

(v) *Conformal and inversive geometry.* Growing spheres map under inversion to spheres or planes, and the family of wavefronts is a pencil in the inversive geometry of space, invariant under the conformal group.

(vi) *Null hypersurfaces.* The five senses above are topological, metric, causal, contact-geometric and conformal. The deepest is Lorentzian. The expanding Sphere in (x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄) with x₄ advancing at ic meets any spatial slice in a sphere of radius growing at c, which is precisely the intersection of a null hypersurface with that slice. Null hypersurfaces are causally extremal — neither spacelike nor timelike — and are the only surfaces along which signals propagate at c. Every point of the Sphere carries the same null-hypersurface identity: all lie on one light cone, connected to the origin and to one another through the null geodesic structure.

The six analyses are mutually reinforcing rather than alternative: each frames one physical object in the language of a different discipline, and each yields the conclusion that the wavefront's spatially separated points share an identity traceable to one local origin. What appears from within a spatial slice as a collection of causally disconnected points is, in the four-dimensional geometry forced by dx₄/dt = ic, one object — in six senses at once.

#### II.29.4.4 The two laws Under dx₄/dt = ic

The Channel B reading admits formalization as two laws [MG-Nonlocality, §2].

**The First McGucken Law of Nonlocality.** *All quantum nonlocality begins in locality.* Two systems can exhibit entanglement only if they have shared a common local origin, or if each has interacted locally with members of a system that itself shared one. Equivalently: only particles whose light spheres intersect, each sphere having originated with its own particle, can be entangled. The creation of entanglement is limited by c, even though the correlations found on measuring an entangled pair are instantaneous and persist under subsequent separation. The First Law constrains the creation of entanglement, not its manifestation.

**The Second McGucken Law of Nonlocality.** *Nonlocality grows in a manner limited by c.* As x₄ expands, the Sphere grows; at parameter t after a local event its radius is r = ct. Particles within it may be entangled with that event and particles outside it may not, because the expansion has not reached them. The boundary of entanglement possibility is exactly the light cone.

The Two Laws connect entanglement directly to the causal structure of spacetime. The expansion of x₄ at c generates simultaneously the light cone (Channel A, through the Minkowski metric), the expanding wavefront of wave optics (Channel B, through Huygens' principle) and the sphere of potential entanglement (Channel B, through the shared Sphere). The Two Laws are the Channel B counterpart of the locality axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, which are Channel A consequences; one principle generates both the local structure and the correlations, along its two disjoint channels.

Remark VIII.23.4 (intersecting Spheres and the transfer of entanglement). The First Law accommodates entanglement swapping. Two pairs are created locally, C with D on a Sphere Σ_CD and E with F on a Sphere Σ_EF; C is carried to one location and interacts locally with A, F is carried to another and interacts locally with B, and a Bell measurement on D and E at an intermediate location is itself a local interaction creating a correlation carried on a third Sphere Σ_DE. The three Spheres intersect pairwise at the two measurement events, and the resulting A–B correlation is carried by that chain. Every link traces back to a local creation event, so the correlation is transferred rather than primitive. Along each Sphere in the chain there is neither proper time nor proper distance between the events it carries: the wavefront is one four-dimensional object however far it extends in a spatial slice.

Remark VIII.23.5 (the falsification criterion). The prediction implicit in the Two Laws is stated in [MG-Nonlocality, §3] as a criterion: to falsify the account one would have to entangle two distant, previously unentangled systems with no chain of local contacts and faster than c. Every known protocol for creating entanglement at a distance — swapping, Bell-measurement mediation, teleportation, cascaded parametric down-conversion, cavity-mediated spin-spin entanglement, and the loophole-free tests with sources and analyzers separated by kilometres — proceeds by a chain of locally originated Spheres, with each intersection a local interaction at which the correlation is transferred. The account predicts that no protocol without such a chain can exist, because the creation of entanglement is a Channel B process requiring a shared Sphere and Channel A confines that Sphere's expansion to the light cone. The boundary of entanglement creation and the boundary of causal contact are then the same surface, which is the content of the criterion.

### II.29.5 The Four Levels Together Under dx₄/dt = ic

The separation of §II.5.8 has now been applied at four levels of description, each addressing a different question about quantum mechanics.

| Level | Question addressed | Channel A reading | Channel B reading | Developed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Formulation | Which formulation of quantum mechanics is primary? | Hamiltonian: operator algebra, Stone's theorem, canonical commutation relation (Propositions H.1–H.5) | Lagrangian: Huygens wavefronts, path measure, Feynman kernel (Propositions L.1–L.6) | §II.12.7 |
| 2. Dynamics | How does a quantum system evolve? | Heisenberg picture: observables carried into the translated frame, Â_H(t) = Û(t)†ÂÛ(t) | Schrödinger picture: the state's wavefront carried forward, \|ψ_S(t)⟩ = Û(t)\|ψ⟩ | §II.29.3, Theorem VIII.23.1 |
| 3. Ontology | What is a quantum object? | Particle aspect: eigenvalue events, quantized exchange, localized detection | Wave aspect: interference, diffraction, λ_dB = h/p | §II.29.2 |
| 4. Causality | How do quantum objects stand to the causal structure of spacetime? | Locality: microcausality, [Ô(x), Ô(y)] = 0 at spacelike separation | Nonlocality: the shared McGucken Sphere, E(a,b) = −cos θ_ab, the Two Laws | §II.29.4 |

The four rows are not four independent observations. Each is the same separation of the Principle's content applied to a different question, and the agreement across the four is what makes the separation itself credible: a distinction drawn to explain one coexistence, which then explains three further coexistences without modification, is doing work rather than being fitted.

The ordering of the rows is one of increasing depth. Level 1 concerns the mathematical machinery used to compute. Level 2 concerns time evolution within a given machinery. Level 3 concerns the character of the object itself. Level 4 concerns how objects stand to the causal structure of spacetime, and is the deepest of the four because the coexistence of locality with nonlocal correlation is precisely the feature Einstein identified in 1935 and Bell analysed in 1964 as the most distinctive of the theory. That one separation of content generates all four coexistences — including the most contested — is what the four-level table is offered as evidence for.

Two consequences follow for the program of the present paper.

The first concerns the reach of Theorem VI.1. The four-fold uniqueness theorem consumes both channels, as the audit in §II.5.8.2 records: Channel A supplies the Poincaré invariance of Proposition IV.1, the Clifford structure and phase indeterminacy of Propositions V.1 and VI.2; Channel B supplies the causal cone that Schuller closure takes as input in Proposition VI.3 and the Compton coupling of the matter orientation condition. A framework carrying one channel could not reach four sectors, for the same reason it could not reach four coexistences.

The second concerns the standing of the whole. By the criterion of §II.29.1.5, a framework is a foundation rather than a reformulation if its principle is not a rewriting of what it derives, if the known results follow as consequences, and if at least one important result is overdetermined. The four instances catalogued there — the commutation relation, Huygens' principle, the Second Law and the Einstein–Hilbert sector — satisfy the third condition four times over. The four levels of the present section show that the property responsible for the overdetermination, namely the presence of two channels in one geometric-dynamical statement, is not a fortunate accident of one derivation but the organizing feature of the framework, visible wherever quantum mechanics presents a pair of coexisting descriptions that the received account leaves unexplained.

## II.30. Two Conceptions of the Foundations of Physics: A Meta-Theory of All Possible Models, and the One Physical Reality From Which the Laws Deduce Under dx₄/dt = ic

Everything below descends from the physical expansion of x₄. The McGucken Principle states that the fourth dimension is expanding at the rate c from every point of spacetime, dx₄/dt = ic. Section VIII.22 set the results of the Assumptions of Physics programme beside the theorems of that Principle terminus by terminus. The present section addresses something prior to any particular terminus: what the two programmes take the word *foundations* to mean. The difference is stated plainly by the programme's own author, it is deliberate, and it accounts for the pattern of §II.28 better than any comparison of individual results does.

Quotations in this section are from the programme's 2025–26 overview lecture [AoP-Overview], whose auto-generated transcript has been lightly repunctuated without alteration of wording; the timestamps are given so that each may be checked against the recording.

### II.30.1 The programme's aim, in its own words Under dx₄/dt = ic

The constructive aim is stated at the opening: "the main goal of assumptions of physics is to identify a handful of physical starting points from which the basic laws can be rigorously derived" (0:11), with the further requirement that the mathematics itself — "real numbers, topology, sigma algebra and all that" (2:08) — be recovered from physical requirements rather than assumed. That aim is Einsteinian in form, and it is the aim §II.28 engages.

The meta-aim is different, and it is stated with equal directness. The received view in the field, as the lecture characterizes it, is "that all the theory that we have right now are approximation of the one true theory," and that "the goal of physics is to find this one true law of the universe" (2:52–2:58). The programme sets that view aside: "saying that the goal of physics is to find the true laws of the universe is not a very productive point" (5:02). What replaces it is stated at 5:36–5:55:

> "the foundations of physics basically mean to find the theory of physical models. Not to find the one true model that rules them all, but is to find a meta theory for all the possible physical models."

The model for that ambition is drawn explicitly from another discipline: "in the foundations of mathematics nobody's looking for the theorem of everything, the theorem that proves all the theorem. No, doing foundations in mathematics means doing logic, doing model theory" (7:03–7:18), with the same point made for the foundations of computer science, where the object of study is what computation is rather than an algorithm that subsumes all algorithms.

The same posture governs the treatment of limits. On the recovery of classical mechanics at high entropy and of non-relativistic mechanics at low speed, the lecture states: "in both cases you see that there is no mechanism for this limit" (37:44), and "there's no mechanism required for being at high entropy" (38:27). The absence of a mechanism is presented as a feature, since it frees the classical limit from any dependence on decoherence or on any other particular process.

None of this is a shortcoming of execution. It is a considered choice of what the subject is, and within that choice the programme's results — the equivalence of the action principle to (DR), (IND) and (KE); the classical uncertainty bound σ_q σ_p ≥ ℏ/e; the recovery of topology and the σ-algebras from experimental verifiability; the identification, at 41:21, that "all the geometric structure that we have in both classical mechanics and quantum mechanics are essentially there exactly to tell you what the entropy of statistical ensembles is" — are rigorous and are, in several cases, results no one else has obtained.

### II.30.2 The other conception, and what deduces from one reality Under dx₄/dt = ic

The conception this paper works within is the older one, and it is the one the programme names as unproductive for its purposes. Einstein put it in 1918, in the address for Planck's sixtieth birthday: "The supreme task of the physicist is to arrive at those universal elementary laws from which the cosmos can be built up by pure deduction" [Einstein 1918]. Wheeler put the same expectation as a prediction about what the answer would feel like when found — "behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, that when we grasp it — in a decade, a century, or a millennium — we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?" — quoted as the epigraph of §II.3 of this paper. Neither statement is a claim about a catalog of possible models. Both are claims that there is one physical reality and that the laws are what follow from it.

The McGucken Principle is a proposal of exactly that kind. It names a physical ontology in one sentence — the fourth dimension is expanding at the rate c from every point of spacetime — and everything the present paper contains is deduction from it. The inventory below is not new material; it is a map of what has already been derived and where, assembled so that the shape of the claim is visible in one place.
